Fact.Name: Form 7206 line 14: the self employed health insurance deduction
Fact.Description:
Form 7206 line 14, the smaller of line 3 and line 13, which the filer carries to Schedule 1 line 17. It models the long term care amount, the SEP and SIMPLE subtraction, the S corporation route and the Form 2555 amount that scheduleSE /selfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction collapses away, so it is the wider computation of the same printed line. Print only until Schedule 1 line 17 reads it. NOT PRINT ONLY: scheduleSE /selfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction (Schedule 1 line 17) now computes its deducting arm as THIS fact, behind the same population guards it always had; lines 2, 9 and 12 read their OrZero wrappers so the chain resolves on every return that reaches it. On the single-profitable-business shape the value is identical to the collapsed LesserOf it replaces (line 6 is 1000/1000, so line 7 is the whole SE-tax deduction and line 13 is Schedule C profit less that deduction); the one population where it differs is a return that also carries K-1 self-employment earnings and attests exactly one business as the plan business (a Schedule C beside a partnership K-1 with box 14 code A profit is refused until then, by scheduleSE /knockoutSelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction), where line 6 prorates the SE-tax deduction by business as the form instructs — the collapsed arm subtracted all of it.
FLOORED AT $0. "The smaller of line 3 or line 13" is negative whenever line 13 is, and line 13 CAN be negative: a loss-making plan business puts its signed loss on line 4 (the multi-business arm this change builds), and on any return line 9's fallback, the WHOLE of Schedule 1 line 16 when the Form 7206 box is blank, can exceed line 8. A negative here would reach Schedule 1 line 17 as a negative deduction and RAISE AGI, which no reading of section 162(l) permits: paragraph (1) allows "an amount equal to the amount paid" and paragraph (2)(A) only ever REDUCES it, so the deduction is bounded below by zero, and the instructions' precondition ("You were self-employed and had a net profit for the year") says the loss-making filer has none. Value-identical on every committed return, none of which has a negative line 13; pinned negative-to-zero by f7206-plan-business-is-the-loss-maker-line-14-floors-at-zero. Also, the multi-business population REACHES this line: scheduleSE /selfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction files it whenever exactly one business is attested as the plan business, and the line 6 proration is then a real ratio, not only the K-1 exception the paragraph above names.
SCHEDULE A COORDINATION (IRC section 162(l)(3)): this figure — the amount actually allowed as the section 162(l) deduction, after the earned-income ceiling — cannot also be taken into account in computing the Schedule A medical expense deduction under section 213(a). This graph holds the coordination on only one side of it today: scheduleSE /selfEmployedHealthInsuranceSingleProfitableBusiness's Description quotes the printed sentence, but that is the Schedule 1 line 17 fact, which no itemiser reads. This fact is the amount a self-employed itemiser must exclude from scheduleA:/writableMedicalExpenses; nothing here computes that exclusion or checks it, because Schedule A's intake is a single filer-entered total with no visibility into this figure. Successor duty, named for whichever unit next touches Schedule A's medical-expense intake: read this fact (form7206:/form7206Line14SelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction) and either disclose the coordination on scheduleA:/writableMedicalExpenses's own Description (the screen the filer who could double-count actually sees) or detect an entered total that appears to include it.

Fact.Name: The partnership or S corporation reported the health insurance premiums as your income
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Help text: "If you are a partner or a more-than-2% S corporation shareholder, the plan counts as established under the business only if the business paid the premiums, or reimbursed you for them, and reported them as guaranteed payments on your Schedule K-1 or as wages in box 1 of your Form W-2. Otherwise the premiums can't be deducted on Form 7206." Asked when: the plan business is a partnership K-1 (/form7206K1PlanBusinessCount above 0) or the filer has Medicare wages from the S corporation (line 11 above $0). Unanswered: nothing changes (the premiums stand as entered). Answered No: line 1 is $0 (/form7206PremiumsNotReportedByTheEntity). Validation: Boolean.

Fact.Description: True when the plan business is a partnership K-1 or the filer has S corporation Medicare wages on line 11, and the filer answered that the business did not report the premiums as guaranteed payments or box 1 wages (/writableForm7206PremiumsReportedByTheEntity No). Fact.Name: Form 7206 line 1: health insurance premiums paid for the business plan
Fact.Description:
Form 7206 line 1, the total paid in 2025 for health insurance coverage established under the trade or business (or the S corporation in which the filer was a more than 2 percent shareholder). The graph already collects this figure as scheduleSE /writableSelfEmployedHealthInsurancePremiumsPaid, the amount Schedule 1 line 17 is built from, so this is that same intake given the printed line it belongs to rather than a second question.
THE SECTION 402(l)(8) COORDINATION. When the filer both claims a retired public safety officer premium exclusion (form1099Rs:/psoPremiumExclusion above $0) and answers this figure above $0, /writableForm7206Line1IncludesPsoPremiums asks directly whether the entered figure already leaves the excluded distribution-paid premiums out. Answering Yes (the entry still includes them) reduces this line by the exclusion, floored at $0, so the same premium dollars are never counted under both section 402(l) and section 162(l); answering No (the entry already excludes them, as the printed line 1 bullet directs) leaves the figure unchanged. Left unanswered on that co-occurrence, /knockoutForm7206PsoPremiumOverlap refuses rather than guessing which of the two is true of the entry. A partner or more-than-2% S corporation shareholder whose premiums the business did not report as guaranteed payments or box 1 wages has no plan established under the business, so line 1 is $0 (/form7206PremiumsNotReportedByTheEntity).

Fact.Name: Whether the Form 7206 line 1 entry already includes the premiums the PSO exclusion covers
Fact.Description:
Asked only when BOTH form1099Rs:/psoPremiumExclusion is above $0 AND scheduleSE:/writableSelfEmployedHealthInsurancePremiumsPaid is above $0 — the co-occurrence /knockoutForm7206PsoPremiumOverlap refuses until this question is answered. Section 402(l)(8) forbids the retired-public-safety-officer distribution exclusion and the section 162(l) premium deduction from ever covering the same dollars; the two figures are computed in different modules that do not read each other, so the graph asks the filer which one already happened.
FULL SCREEN SPEC (an application engineer builds this screen from this Description without opening an IRS document). SCREEN: "Public safety officer premiums" (new screen, shown immediately after the Form 7206 line 1 premiums-paid question on a return that carries both a positive PSO exclusion and a positive line 1 entry). QUESTION: "Does the amount you entered for your self-employed health insurance premiums include the premiums you paid using your retired public safety officer distribution exclusion?" HELP TEXT: "Form 7206 line 1's own instructions ask you to leave out up to $3,000 of premiums paid from retirement plan distributions that were nontaxable because you are a retired public safety officer — those dollars cannot also be deducted here. Answer No if the amount you entered already leaves those distribution-paid premiums out, as the line 1 instructions direct. Answer Yes only if the amount you entered still includes them — for example, if you were not sure they needed to be left out, or you are not sure which premiums your entry covers." CONTROL: single Yes/No toggle, no default. ASKED WHEN: form1099Rs:/psoPremiumExclusion Complete and above $0, AND scheduleSE:/writableSelfEmployedHealthInsurancePremiumsPaid Complete and above $0. UNANSWERED POSTURE: REFUSED. /knockoutForm7206PsoPremiumOverlap blocks submission until this is answered; there is no safe default, since a wrong guess in either direction either double-subtracts a filer who already excluded the overlap or lets a filer who did not exclude it deduct the same premiums twice. VALIDATION: Boolean, no further validation. WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: form7206:/form7206Line1HealthInsurancePremiums. No leaves line 1 exactly as entered. Yes reduces line 1 by form1099Rs:/psoPremiumExclusion, floored at $0, so the excluded dollars are removed exactly once from the figure that reaches Form 7206 lines 3 and 14 and Schedule 1 line 17. SOURCE: 2025 Form 7206 line 1, second bullet (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f7206.pdf, page 1, "Any amounts paid, not to exceed $3,000, from retirement plan distributions that were nontaxable because you are a retired public safety officer. See instructions."); IRC 402(l)(8) (26 U.S.C. 402, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section402&num=0&edition=2024); 2025 Instructions for Form 1040, Line 17 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 95, FIRST column).

Fact.Name: Form 7206 line 1 PSO overlap answer, complete-safe Boolean
Refuses a return where the PSO premium exclusion and the Form 7206 line 1 entry co-occur and the overlap question is unanswered
Fact.Description:
Refuses a self-employed return that BOTH computed a positive retired public safety officer (PSO) premium exclusion (form1099Rs:/psoPremiumExclusion, the per-filer $3,000-capped amount IRC section 402(l)(8) forbids taking into account under section 162(l) a second time) AND answered Form 7206 line 1 (scheduleSE:/writableSelfEmployedHealthInsurancePremiumsPaid) above $0, while /writableForm7206Line1IncludesPsoPremiums — the question asking whether the line 1 entry already leaves the excluded distribution-paid premiums out — remains unanswered.
THE POPULATION. A retired public safety officer with a profitable trade or business who is also paying self-employed health insurance premiums, and who has not yet said whether the entered premium figure already excludes the distribution-paid amount. Section 402(l)(8) is a hard rule, not a filer election: whatever premium dollars the retirement-distribution exclusion already covered can never also be a section 162(l) premium, and the two figures are computed in different modules that do not read each other, so the graph must ask.
RESIDUE, AND WHY IT IS PERMANENT. Once /writableForm7206Line1IncludesPsoPremiums is answered, form7206:/form7206Line1HealthInsurancePremiums reads it directly: No leaves line 1 exactly as entered (the filer already excluded the overlap, per the printed line 1 bullet); Yes reduces line 1 by the exclusion, floored at $0. Both answers resolve the return without this guard. What remains refused is pure data completeness: the two positive amounts co-occur and the filer has not yet said which of the two is true of their entry. No computation can supply that answer — it depends on how the filer actually filled out the box, not on anything else this graph knows — so the remedy is always the filer answering the question, never a derivation. Same class as the HSA "unanswered coverage months" guard: a permanent, non-narrowing refusal over an unanswered intake.

Fact.Name: Form 7206 line 4: net profit of the business the plan is established under
Fact.Description: Form 7206 line 4, the net profit and other earned income of the trade or business under which the insurance plan is established. TWO ARMS. When exactly one business is attested as the plan business (/form7206PlanEstablishingBusinessAttestedExactlyOne, over the per-Schedule-C, per-partnership-K-1 and Schedule F attestations) this is THAT business's own figure, /form7206AttestedPlanBusinessNetProfit: its Schedule C line 31, its box 14 code A earnings, or Schedule F line 34, signed. Otherwise the fallback is /form7206Line5ScheduleCTerm, the profitable Schedule C businesses' line 31s with losses dropped, which on the single-profitable-business population is exactly the one profitable business's own line 31. A second profitable business is not refused outright: with exactly one attestation it COMPUTES, line 6 becomes a real ratio, and scheduleSE /selfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction files the result; without exactly one attestation it is still refused by scheduleSE /knockoutSelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction. A LOSS-MAKING PLAN BUSINESS reaches this line signed and negative, as "your net profit" of that business; line 6 floors the ratio at 0.000 and line 14 floors the deduction at $0, because the instructions' precondition for the deduction is a net profit from the plan business. Not modelled on either arm and named on /form7206AttestedPlanBusinessNetProfit: the optional-method substitution in the footnote, "any other earned income", and the Conservation Reserve Program exclusion. Line 4 also adds the other earned income from that business the filer reports (/form7206Line4OtherEarnedIncomeOrZero, footnote **: gains from the sale, transfer or licensing of property the filer created, not capital gain).

Fact.Name: Form 7206 line 5: total net profits of all profitable businesses
Fact.Description:
Form 7206 line 5, the total of all net profits from Schedule C line 31, Schedule F line 34 and Schedule K-1 box 14 code A. The Schedule F and Schedule K-1 terms are floored at zero so losses drop out as the printed line requires; the Schedule C term is scheduleC /scheduleCNetProfit, which nets several Schedule C businesses against each other and therefore equals the printed line exactly on the single profitable business population this form is rendered for.
THE SCHEDULE C TERM is /form7206Line5ScheduleCTerm: each Schedule C business's own line 31 floored at zero before the total, the working interest floored the same way. A NET figure would equal the printed line only on the single profitable business population; on a multi-business return, or a single-profitable return with a loss-making Schedule C beside it, netting would drop the denominator below the printed "total of all net profits" and overstate the line 6 ratio. Pinned by f7206-one-profit-one-loss-unattested-line-4-is-the-profitable-business and exercised by f7206-plan-business-is-the-loss-maker-line-14-floors-at-zero. STILL NOT MODELLED, named here because the printed line names them: "any other income allocable to the profitable businesses", the optional-method substitution of the footnote, and the Conservation Reserve Program exclusion.

Fact.Name: Form 7206 line 6 in thousandths, as the division and rounding nodes first produce it
Fact.Description: 1000 times line 4 divided by line 5, rounded to a whole number of thousandths, capped at 1000 and floored at 0, when line 5 is above $0; $0 otherwise. This is an intermediate figure and not the printed line. A Dollar division is reduced to cents (half to even) before the outer Round takes it to whole thousandths (half up), so a true quotient a fraction of a cent below one half of a thousandth is rounded up; the cent reduction moves a value by at most half a cent, so the only possible error here is one thousandth too high. /form7206Line6BusinessProfitRatioThousandths corrects that step with exact cent arithmetic.

Fact.Name: Form 7206 line 6: line 4 divided by line 5, in thousandths
Fact.Description:
Form 7206 line 6, line 4 divided by line 5, carried as thousandths so the printed three decimal box and the line 7 apportionment read the same number. It is 1000 (that is, 1.000) whenever the plan's business is the only profitable one, which is the population this dictionary computes.
NO LONGER ONLY 1.000: with exactly one business attested as the plan business on a multi-business return this is a real ratio, the attested business's own net profit over the total of all profitable businesses, and line 7 apportions the self-employment-tax deduction by it as the printed line instructs. FLOORED AT 0.000 in the same edit: a loss-making plan business puts a negative line 4 over a positive line 5, and a negative ratio would turn line 7 into an addition; the deduction is nil for that filer (line 14 floors at $0), so the apportioned share is nil too. ROUNDING IS THIS DICTIONARY'S, NOT THE FORM'S: neither the printed line ("Divide line 4 by line 5") nor the Instructions for Form 7206, which carry no line-by-line text at all, state a number of decimal places, so the three-place rounding of the Thousandths idiom is kept as the register's convention and the printed box shows it; tagged ai-only for that reason. The printed decimal is ONE half-up rounding of the true quotient: this fact starts from /form7206Line6RatioRoundedAfterCentSnap and steps it down by one thousandth exactly when 2,000 times line 4 (floored at zero) is less than (2 times that figure minus 1) times line 5, the exact cent comparison saying the true quotient is below the lower half-thousandth boundary. Every product in that comparison is a whole number of cents, so no rounding enters the test.

Fact.Name: Form 7206 line 7: deductible part of self employment tax times the line 6 percentage
Fact.Description: Form 7206 line 7, Schedule 1 line 15 (scheduleSE /selfEmploymentTaxDeduction) multiplied by the line 6 fraction, computed as Round(Divide(Multiply(line 15, line 6 thousandths), 1000)) — the shape form2555Housing /form2555ComputedLine36HousingExclusion already uses for the same thousandths idiom. Multiplying first and dividing once keeps the product of two whole-dollar figures exact, so the single division carries the full ratio (a line 6 fraction other than 1000/1000 is preserved to the thousandth rather than rounded to cents before the multiply). Pinned by f7206-two-schedule-c-plan-under-one-real-ratio (2402 times 408 over 1000, 980), f7206-plan-under-partnership-k1-beside-a-schedule-c (1403 times 302 over 1000, 424) and f7206-plan-under-schedule-f-beside-a-schedule-c (1837 times 467 over 1000, 858). The printed line has no rounding words of its own beyond "the percentage on line 6"; the whole-dollar Round is the register's convention. ONE-DOLLAR EDGE, DISCLOSED NOT FIXED: the single Divide still passes a cents intermediate (HALF_EVEN) before the whole-dollar HALF_UP Round, so when line 15 times line 6 is congruent to 495 modulo 1000 the figure rounds twice, e.g. 2,999 times 505 = 1,514,495 gives exact 1,514.495, cents 1,514.50, then 1,515 where exact whole-dollar rounding gives 1,514. At most $1, reachable only at that residue, and the same shape as form2555Housing /form2555ComputedLine36HousingExclusion.

Fact.Name: Form 7206 line 11: Medicare wages from the S corporation the plan is established under
Fact.Description:
Form 7206 line 11, box 5 Medicare wages from an S corporation in which the filer is a more than 2 percent shareholder and in which the insurance plan is established (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f7206.pdf, page 1). THIS FACT, the hand entered total, is the line 11 wrapper's (/form7206Line11SCorporationMedicareWagesOrZero) KEPT FALLBACK, NOT THE PREFERRED SHAPE, for a return where the per W-2 question was never asked: the preferred shape is the per-W-2 attribution, /formW2s/*/writableForm7206IsSCorporationMoreThanTwoPercentShareholder (the flag naming which employer it is), /formW2s/*/form7206SCorporationMedicareWagesOrZero (that W-2's contribution) and /form7206Line11SCorporationMedicareWagesFromW2s (the total over the flagged W-2s). It is kept rather than retired because the flag is intake surface with no screen behind it, so a return migrated from the old shape would otherwise lose its line 11 outright.
IT IS NOT PRINT ONLY. /form7206Line11SCorporationMedicareWagesOrZero reads this entry as its fallback arm, /form7206Line13BaseBeforeExclusion takes that wrapper on the S corporation arm, and line 13 reaches line 14, scheduleSE /selfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction, Schedule 1 line 17 and AGI. scheduleSE /knockoutSelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction's S corporation arm is All(IsComplete(x), x, Not(/form7206Line11SCorporationWagesAttributedFromW2s)): a return that flags EXACTLY ONE Form W-2 as the S corporation's and carries its box 5 is computed, printed AND FILED - Schedule 1 line 17 reads Form 7206 line 14 for it. "Computed and printed but blocked from submission" is true only of the residue: no W-2 flagged (unasked, or answered no on every one), a flagged W-2 whose box 5 is unanswered, a flagged W-2 whose box b ein is unanswered, or flagged W-2s from MORE THAN ONE employer. Several flagged W-2s that share one ein are one corporation and DO file, on the sum of their box 5 amounts.
THE PRINTED BOX IS POINTED HERE: dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS7206/en/configuration.yml f1_13[0] maps /form7206Line11SCorporationMedicareWagesOrZero, so the printed line 11 agrees with the line 13 arm that reads it (fixture f7206-line11-s-corp-wages-read-off-the-flagged-w2-not-the-typed-total).

Fact.Name: Form 7206 line 2: qualified long term care premiums after the age based limit
Fact.Description:
Form 7206 line 2, the total of the per person amounts for coverage under a qualified long term care insurance contract, each the smaller of the payments made for that person or the age banded amount the printed line lists. The age banded table is applied per covered person by the FILER before typing this figure, so the number entered here is already capped in the filer's head and this fact cannot check it.
THE PER COVERED PERSON SHAPE (owner direction): /filers/*/writableForm7206LongTermCarePremiumsPaid is the per person payment intake, /filers/*/form7206LongTermCarePremiumAgeBandLimit reads the five printed bands off filers:/filers/*/age, /filers/*/form7206LongTermCarePremiumAfterAgeLimit is the printed smaller of, and /form7206Line2LongTermCarePremiumsPerPersonTotal totals them; this return-level figure is the fallback. scheduleSE /selfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction consumes Form 7206 line 14, so this is not a print only chain.
THIS SCALAR IS THE KEPT FALLBACK, NOT THE PREFERRED SHAPE. /form7206Line2LongTermCarePremiumsOrZero takes the per person total whenever any filer answered the per person intake and falls back to this entry otherwise. It is kept rather than retired because the computed arm covers FILERS only, while the printed line covers any person the contract covers, including a dependent, for whom no per person intake exists yet. IT REMAINS UNCLAMPED, which is the disclosed divergence the scheduleSE /selfEmployedLongTermCarePremiumAgeLimit contract asks the project owner to rule on, now confined to the population the per person intake cannot reach.
THE PRINTED BOX IS POINTED HERE: dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS7206/en/configuration.yml f1_4[0] now maps /form7206Line2LongTermCarePremiumsOrZero (the f1_14[0] re-point precedent and comment shape), so the printed line 2 agrees with the lines 3/14 arithmetic. STILL TRUE AFTER THE ARM 3 NARROWING, and it is the reason /form7206Line11SCorporationWagesAttributedFromW2s requires EXACTLY ONE EMPLOYER among the flagged W-2s rather than at least one flagged W-2: two flagged W-2s from two different employers would total both corporations' box 5 into one line 11 against one line 1, taxpayer favourably and silently. Optional: unanswered on every W-2 means the question was never asked, and line 11 then falls back to the hand entered total.

Fact.Name: The Form 7206 S corporation question was answered on this W-2
Fact.Description: Whether /formW2s/*/writableForm7206IsSCorporationMoreThanTwoPercentShareholder was answered on THIS W-2, true or false. The per item half of the answered-ness predicate the line 11 wrapper switches on, kept as its own complete safe Boolean so the return level Count never counts an Incomplete item. IT TESTS ANSWERED, NOT TRUE, and the difference is the point of the rewire: a filer who was asked the question and said no on every W-2 has told the return there are no S corporation wages, so line 11 is $0 for them even if the old hand entered total holds a figure. That is the audit's finding acted on, and it agrees with the reporting adverse default the line 11 wrapper already documents. Added by operator direction.

Fact.Name: This W-2's box 5 when it is the S corporation W-2, else 0
Fact.Description: The Form 7206 line 11 term this W-2 contributes: formW2s /formW2s/*/medicareWagesUnrounded when the filer flagged this W-2 as the more than 2 percent S corporation's, and $0 otherwise. CENTS ARE PRESERVED HERE ON PURPOSE. This is an ADDEND, not a printed entry, and the total above it rounds once: it is the round-once-at-the-total shape formW2s /formW2totalMedicareWages ships, which the i1040gi rule requires ("If you have to add two or more amounts to figure the amount to enter on a line, include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total"). Summing already rounded per W-2 box 5 amounts would mis state line 11 by up to about $0.50 per extra W-2. Complete safe twice over: the flag arm falls to $0 when the question was not answered or was answered false, and the amount it reads is itself the complete safe box 5 wrapper. Added by operator direction.

Fact.Name: Form 7206 line 11 computed: box 5 totalled over the flagged W-2s
Fact.Description: Form 7206 line 11 read off the Forms W-2 the return already files: the total of box 5 over the W-2s the filer flagged as the more than 2 percent S corporation's, summed with cents and rounded once at this printed line. This is the shape the scheduleSE /selfEmployedHealthInsuranceSCorpMedicareWagesCeiling contract asks for, and it replaces asking the filer for a number the return holds; the hand entered total is kept only as the fallback for a return where the flag was never asked. WHY THE COLLECTION IS GUARDED RATHER THAN SUMMED RAW: /formW2s is genuinely empty on returns with no wage income, and this is scheduleC /scheduleCNetProfit's shipping shape used verbatim rather than trusting empty collection sum semantics, so line 13, line 14 and AGI cannot go Incomplete on such a return. $0 on every committed return, because no W-2 in the corpus carries the flag. NO BODY CHANGE, and the reason this sum is SAFE TO FILE is worth stating where the sum lives. /form7206Line11SCorporationWagesAttributedFromW2s, the predicate scheduleSE /knockoutSelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction's arm 3 is narrowed by, admits a return only when every flagged W-2 shares ONE formW2s /formW2s/*/ein. On that population "the total over the flagged W-2s" IS "the total over the W-2s of the one S corporation", which is the ONE line 11 of the ONE Form 7206 the printed note requires, and the Round wrapper still rounds ONCE at the end rather than per row (pinned: box 5 of 46,282.49 and 60,000.49 on two same-EIN flagged W-2s file line 11 = 106,283.00, not the 106,282.00 that per-row rounding would give). Flagged W-2s with DIFFERENT EINs are two plan corporations and stay refused, so this fact still PRINTS their merged total and the return still cannot be submitted - consumed is not the same as filed.

Fact.Name: The Form 7206 S corporation question was answered on some W-2
Fact.Description: Whether the filer answered /formW2s/*/writableForm7206IsSCorporationMoreThanTwoPercentShareholder on at least one Form W-2. This is the answered-ness predicate the line 11 wrapper switches on, and it is why the promoted hand entered total can be kept as a fallback rather than retired: when the question was never asked the wrapper falls through to that total and the return reads exactly as it did before. Guarded in the same shape as the sum beside it so an empty or Incomplete /formW2s reads FALSE rather than propagating. FALSE on every committed return, which is the byte identical argument. Added by operator direction.

Fact.Name: This W-2 is flagged as the S corporation's
Fact.Description: Whether /formW2s/*/writableForm7206IsSCorporationMoreThanTwoPercentShareholder was answered TRUE on THIS W-2 — the per item half of the attribution predicate below. IT TESTS TRUE, NOT ANSWERED, and that is the whole difference from /formW2s/*/form7206SCorporationShareholderFlagAnswered beside it: a filer who was asked and said no on every W-2 has answered the question, but no wages are attributed to the S corporation and Form 7206 line 11 is $0. Complete safe: false when the question was never asked on this W-2, so an unasked W-2 can never make the return level count Incomplete.

Fact.Name: This W-2 is flagged as the S corporation's but carries no box 5
Fact.Description: Whether this W-2 was flagged as the more than 2 percent S corporation's AND formW2s /formW2s/*/writableMedicareWages was never answered on it. WHY THIS IS A REFUSAL TERM RATHER THAN A ROUNDING DETAIL: formW2s /formW2s/*/medicareWagesUnrounded is complete safe to $0, so an unanswered box 5 on a FLAGGED W-2 silently contributes nothing to /form7206Line11SCorporationMedicareWagesFromW2s. The return has said "these are the S corporation's wages" and then not said what they are, so the section 162(l)(2)(A) ceiling is unknown rather than zero; filing it as zero UNDERSTATES the deduction, and the direction is the only reason nobody complains. The return level predicate below turns this into the honest data completeness residue scheduleSE /knockoutSelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction keeps on its third arm. Complete safe: false when the flag was never answered or was answered false.

Fact.Name: The first Form W-2 flagged as the S corporation's
Fact.Description: The first Form W-2 on the return whose /formW2s/*/writableForm7206IsSCorporationMoreThanTwoPercentShareholder was answered TRUE, used ONLY as the employer identification number the other flagged W-2s are compared against by /formW2s/*/form7206SCorporationW2FlaggedForADifferentEmployer beside it. WHY A Find AND NOT A COUNT: Form 7206 is one form per plan BUSINESS, not per Form W-2, so the question line 11 actually asks is how many EMPLOYERS the flagged wages come from, and the discriminator formW2s /formW2s/*/ein already ships on every W-2. Comparing every flagged W-2 to this one is what turns "exactly one flagged row" into "exactly one flagged employer": all flagged rows equal to it means one S corporation, which is one Form 7206 and one line 11. Incomplete when NO W-2 is flagged, which is why every reader of it fences on IsComplete first.

Fact.Name: This W-2 is flagged as the S corporation's but carries no box b EIN
Fact.Description: Whether this W-2 was flagged as the more than 2 percent S corporation's AND formW2s /formW2s/*/ein was never answered on it. THIS IS A REFUSAL TERM FOR THE SAME REASON THE MISSING BOX 5 IS ONE: the employer identification number is the only thing on the return that says whether two flagged W-2s are one corporation or two, so a flagged W-2 without it cannot be cleared into either the same-employer sum or the two-corporations refusal. Not clearable is refused, never guessed. Complete safe: false when the flag was never answered or was answered false, so an unasked W-2 can never make the return level count Incomplete.

Fact.Name: This flagged W-2 is a SECOND employer beside the first flagged one
Fact.Description: Whether this W-2 is flagged as the more than 2 percent S corporation's and its formW2s /formW2s/*/ein DIFFERS from the ein of /form7206FirstSCorporationFlaggedW2. Zero of these on a return means every flagged W-2 came from ONE employer, which is ONE S corporation, ONE plan business and therefore ONE Form 7206 with ONE line 11 - so their box 5 amounts may be summed. One or more of these means two plan corporations, which the printed form requires to be two separate Forms 7206 ("Note: Use a separate Form 7206 for each trade or business under which an insurance plan is established", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f7206.pdf, page 1) and which this singleton module does not model; that return stays refused by scheduleSE /knockoutSelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction, the same residue arm 1 keeps for a plan-establishing attestation count of two or more. COMPLETE SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION AND IN THAT ORDER: the flag, then IsComplete on this W-2's ein, then IsComplete on the first flagged W-2's ein, and only then the comparison, so a missing ein anywhere makes the All Complete FALSE rather than Incomplete - the missing-ein return is refused by /formW2s/*/form7206SCorporationW2FlaggedWithoutEmployerIdentificationNumber beside it instead, which is the honest place for it.

Fact.Name: Form 7206 line 11 is genuinely read off EXACTLY ONE S corporation
Fact.Description: Whether the Forms W-2 flagged as the more than 2 percent S corporation's come from EXACTLY ONE employer, every one of them carries its box 5 amount, and every one of them carries its box b employer identification number. This is the predicate scheduleSE /knockoutSelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction's third arm is narrowed by, and it is DELIBERATELY STRICTER than /form7206Line11SCorporationQuestionAnswered beside it, which the line 11 wrapper switches on. The wrapper's question is "which source do I read", and answered-no-on-every-W-2 correctly answers it with $0. THIS fact's question is "does the return actually carry the section 162(l)(2)(A) ceiling", and answered-no-on-every-W-2 does NOT: such a return has an S corporation plan attested on scheduleSE /writableSelfEmployedHealthPlanUnderSCorp, a line 11 of $0, a line 13 of $0 and a Form 7206 line 14 of $0, so freeing it would file a wrong ZERO on Schedule 1 line 17 rather than compute one. The same is true of a flagged W-2 whose box 5 was never answered. Both populations stay refused, which is where they already are. ONE EMPLOYER, NOT ONE ROW. The predicate first read "exactly one flagged ROW", on the ground that nothing on the return said whether two flagged W-2s shared an employer. THAT GROUND WAS FALSE ABOUT THE TREE: formW2s /formW2s/*/ein ships on every Form W-2 and is exported to MeF, so the return says exactly that. The two residues it was hiding are now separated and each answered on its own merits. (a) SEVERAL FLAGGED W-2s THAT SHARE ONE EIN are one corporation - a W-2c or a mid-year EIN-preserving payroll change - so they are ONE plan business, ONE Form 7206 and ONE line 11, and /form7206Line11SCorporationMedicareWagesFromW2s already totals exactly those rows, rounding once at the end. That return now FILES; the count of /formW2s/*/form7206SCorporationW2FlaggedForADifferentEmployer is zero on it. (b) FLAGGED W-2s WITH DIFFERENT EINs are two plan corporations, and the printed form requires a separate Form 7206 for each ("Note: Use a separate Form 7206 for each trade or business under which an insurance plan is established", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f7206.pdf, page 1), which this singleton module does not model: totalling both corporations' box 5 into ONE line 11 sitting against ONE line 1 is taxpayer favourable and silent, because the smaller of a summed line 3 and a summed line 13 is never LESS than the sum of the two separate smaller-ofs. That return stays REFUSED, and it is the SAME residue arm 1 already keeps for a plan-establishing attestation count of two or more, on the same authority. It is also the shape the flag's own Description names: "A joint return on which BOTH spouses run S corporations with their own plans is the same multi form shape line 4 and line 6 already do not model, and it stays refused by scheduleSE /knockoutSelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction". (c) A FLAGGED W-2 WHOSE EIN IS UNANSWERED cannot be cleared into either (a) or (b), so it is REFUSED - not clearable is never guessed. GUARDED IN THE SHIPPING COLLECTION SHAPE (scheduleC /scheduleCNetProfit's, used verbatim by the facts beside this one) so an empty or Incomplete /formW2s reads FALSE rather than propagating: a self employed filer with no wage income at all is exactly such a return, and it must reach the refusal rather than an Incomplete. FALSE on every committed return, because no W-2 in the corpus carries the flag.

Fact.Name: The health insurance plan is established under THIS Schedule C business
Fact.Description: Whether the health insurance plan whose premiums Form 7206 line 1 carries is established under THIS sole proprietorship, the attestation the printed form's per-business rule needs ("Use a separate Form 7206 for each trade or business under which an insurance plan is established") and the only thing about the plan's business that no other fact can tell. For a Schedule C business the policy may be in the name of the business or of the individual (Instructions for Form 7206, "For self-employed individuals filing a Schedule C (Form 1040) or Schedule F (Form 1040), a policy can be either in the name of the business or in the name of the individual"), so the question is which business the plan belongs to, not whose name is on it. THE ANSWER CANNOT BE INFERRED: two profitable businesses give two candidate line 4 figures and two ratios on line 6, and picking the larger overstates Schedule 1 line 17 silently. ONE PLAN, ONE BUSINESS: a return that attests more than one business across the Schedule Cs, the partnership K-1s and Schedule F has described the "more than one health plan and business" case the instructions send to SEPARATE Forms 7206, which this singleton module does not model, so /form7206PlanEstablishingBusinessAttestedExactlyOne is false and a multi-business return stays refused. Optional: unanswered on every business means the question was never asked, and line 4 then falls back to the single-profitable-business reading it always had.

Fact.Name: This Schedule C business is the attested plan business (complete safe)
Fact.Description: Whether ../writableForm7206PlanEstablishedUnderThisBusiness was answered TRUE on this Schedule C item. The per item half of the exactly-one test, kept as its own complete safe Boolean so the return level Count never counts an Incomplete item (Count propagates an Incomplete member): unanswered and answered no both read FALSE. It tests ATTESTED, not answered, because what line 4 needs is the identity of the plan business, and a no on every business is the same absence as never asking.

Fact.Name: Form 7206 line 5 term: THIS Schedule C business's line 31, profit only
Fact.Description: This sole proprietorship's own Schedule C line 31 (scheduleC ../netProfit) floored at zero, the per-business term the printed line 5 adds: "Enter the total of all net profits* from Schedule C (Form 1040), line 31 ... Don't include any net losses shown on these schedules". The floor is per BUSINESS on purpose: netting a loss-making Schedule C against a profitable one, which scheduleC /scheduleCNetProfit does because that is what Schedule 1 line 3 wants, understates this denominator and overstates the line 6 ratio, exactly the defect the records contract warns a build against.

Fact.Name: Form 7206 line 4 term: THIS Schedule C business's line 31 when it is the attested plan business, else 0
Fact.Description: This sole proprietorship's own Schedule C line 31 (scheduleC ../netProfit), SIGNED, when the filer attested the plan is established under it, and $0 otherwise. Signed because line 4 is "your net profit" of that one business and a loss-making plan business has none: the negative figure flows to lines 6 (floored at 0.000), 8, 10 and 13, and line 14 floors the deduction at $0, which is what the instructions' precondition requires ("One of the following statements must be true. You were self-employed and had a net profit for the year reported on Schedule C (Form 1040) or Schedule F (Form 1040)"). Summed over the collection by /form7206ScheduleCPlanBusinessNetProfit; with exactly one attested business the sum IS that business's figure.

Fact.Name: The health insurance plan is established under THIS partnership (Schedule K-1)
Fact.Description: Whether the health insurance plan whose premiums Form 7206 line 1 carries is established under the partnership THIS Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) reports, the per-business attestation for the third source the printed line 5 names, "Schedule K-1 (Form 1065), box 14, code A". The instructions state when a partner's plan counts as established under the partnership: "a policy can be either in the name of the" / "partnership or in the name of the partner" and, if in the partner's name, "the partnership must reimburse you and report the" / "premium amounts on Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) as guaranteed" / "payments"; that test is the filer's to apply before answering. ASK ONLY ON A PARTNERSHIP K-1: a plan under an S corporation takes the line 11 route (scheduleSE /writableSelfEmployedHealthPlanUnderSCorp and the per W-2 flag), never line 4, so ../form7206PlanEstablishedUnderThisPartnership withholds an answer given on a K-1 whose entity type is an answered sCorp. Optional: unanswered means this K-1 was not asked.

Fact.Name: This K-1 is the attested plan business, and it is a recorded partnership K-1 (complete safe)
Fact.Description: Whether ../writableForm7206PlanEstablishedUnderThisPartnership was answered TRUE on this K-1 AND the K-1 is not recorded as an S corporation (scheduleE ../k1EntityTypeAnsweredSCorp, which is true only for an ANSWERED sCorp, the module's own three-state idiom). The S corporation exclusion is the printed form's: "If the business is an S corporation, skip to line 11", so an S corporation can never be the line 4 business, and an attestation typed onto one is withheld rather than counted; on a multi-business return that leaves the count short and the return refused, which is the honest reading of a contradictory intake. Complete safe: an unanswered attestation, an answered no, or an unrecorded entity type with a no all read FALSE, and the shape is All(IsComplete, value, Not(sCorp)), which resolves Complete false as soon as any member is. CORRECTED: the third conjunct is now the POSITIVE scheduleE ../k1EntityTypeAnsweredPartnership (All(IsComplete(../entityType), Equal(partnership)), the module's own three-state idiom), not Not(../k1EntityTypeAnsweredSCorp). The sentence above that says an unrecorded type "with a no" reads false was true but incomplete: a YES on a K-1 whose entity type was never recorded also counted, and "I did not say what kind of K-1 this is" is not a statement that it came from a partnership. Now an unrecorded type withholds the attestation exactly as an answered S corporation does; the S corporation exclusion above is unchanged in effect. Value-neutral: no committed K-1 attests.

Fact.Name: Form 7206 line 4 term: THIS K-1's box 14 code A earnings when it is the attested plan business, else 0
Fact.Description: This partnership K-1's box 14 code A self-employment earnings as declared (scheduleE ../seEarnings, the complete safe signed alias), when the filer attested the plan is established under this partnership, and $0 otherwise. It reads the DECLARED figure rather than ../seEarningsAllowed on purpose: the allowed figure goes Incomplete on a declared loss whose deductible part is unstated, and that return is already refused by scheduleE /knockoutK1NegativeSeEarnings, so reading it here would only turn an honest refusal into an Incomplete Schedule 1 line 17 and AGI; a declared loss reaches line 4 signed either way and line 14 floors the deduction at $0. Summed over the collection by /form7206K1PlanBusinessSeEarnings.

Fact.Name: The health insurance plan is established under the Schedule F farm business
Fact.Description: Whether the health insurance plan whose premiums Form 7206 line 1 carries is established under the farming business Schedule F reports, the per-business attestation for the second source the printed line 5 names, "Schedule F (Form 1040), line 34". RETURN LEVEL, NOT PER ITEM, because Schedule F is a singleton in this dictionary: scheduleF /scheduleFNetProfitOrLoss is one return-level line 34 and scheduleF.xml carries no farm collection (its only Collection is the Form 1099-PATR document store), so there is exactly one farm business to attest and this Boolean is its item. If a farm collection is ever built this moves onto its items in the shape /scheduleCs/*/writableForm7206PlanEstablishedUnderThisBusiness has. Optional: unanswered means the question was not asked and the farm contributes nothing to the attestation count.

Fact.Name: The Schedule F farm is the attested plan business (complete safe)
Fact.Description: Whether /writableForm7206PlanEstablishedUnderScheduleF was answered TRUE. Complete safe in the All(IsComplete, value) shape: unanswered and answered no both read FALSE.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Form 7206 on a return whose farm is a qualified joint venture
Fact.Description: Blocks submission when the Schedule F farm is a qualified joint venture the spouses elected (scheduleF:/scheduleFIsQualifiedJointVenture) AND the return files Form 7206 (/form7206RequiredForReturn). THE WRONG NUMBER IT PREVENTS: a qualified joint venture splits the farm so each spouse files a separate Schedule F carrying only that spouse's share, and the section 162(l)(2)(A) earned income ceiling is measured on the self-employed individual's own income. This module is one return-level Form 7206 and reads the COMBINED farm figure (/form7206ScheduleFNetProfitOrLossSafe) on line 4 when the plan is established under the farm and on line 5 always, so the ceiling counts the other spouse's share: directly on line 4, and through a line 6 ratio that is too low on line 5, which shrinks the line 7 self-employment tax share and raises line 8. Every return without an elected qualified joint venture, and every one that files no Form 7206, is unaffected. SCREEN: "You and your spouse elected to treat your farm as a qualified joint venture, and you are deducting self-employed health insurance. The deduction limit depends on your own share of the farm's profit, and this product figures it on the whole farm, so this return cannot be filed here." COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE: the joint venture gate is unconditionally Complete and Form 7206's own gate is read after its completeness test.

Fact.Name: Form 7206 line 4 term: Schedule F line 34 when the farm is the attested plan business, else 0
Fact.Description: Schedule F line 34 (through /form7206ScheduleFNetProfitOrLossSafe, the complete safe wrapper), SIGNED, when the filer attested the plan is established under the farm, and $0 otherwise. Signed for the same reason as the Schedule C term: a loss-making plan business has no net profit and line 14 floors the deduction at $0.

Fact.Name: How many Schedule C businesses are attested as the plan business
Fact.Description: The Count of /scheduleCs/*/form7206PlanEstablishedUnderThisBusiness, guarded in the module's collection shape (IsComplete and a nonempty /scheduleCs, else 0) so a return with no Schedule C reads 0 rather than propagating. One term of /form7206PlanEstablishingBusinessCount.

Fact.Name: How many partnership K-1s are attested as the plan business
Fact.Description: The Count of /formK1s/*/form7206PlanEstablishedUnderThisPartnership (which already excludes an answered S corporation K-1), guarded in the module's collection shape so a return with no K-1 reads 0. One term of /form7206PlanEstablishingBusinessCount.

Fact.Name: Whether the Schedule F farm is attested as the plan business, as a count (0 or 1)
Fact.Description: 1 when /form7206PlanEstablishedUnderScheduleF is true, else 0, so the singleton farm adds to /form7206PlanEstablishingBusinessCount in the same units as the two collection counts.

Fact.Name: How many businesses on this return are attested as the one the health insurance plan is established under
Fact.Description: The attestation count across the three sources the printed line 5 names: attested Schedule C items, attested partnership K-1 items (S corporation K-1s excluded) and the Schedule F farm. Form 7206 is one form per plan business, so the number this module can compute for is exactly 1 (/form7206PlanEstablishingBusinessAttestedExactlyOne). 0 is "nobody was asked, or every business said no"; 2 or more is the "more than one health plan and business" case the instructions send to separate Forms 7206, which this singleton module does not model. Both are the data-completeness residue scheduleSE /knockoutSelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction refuses on a multi-business return. Complete safe: every term is.

Fact.Name: Exactly one business is attested as the plan business, so Form 7206 line 4 is that business's own figure
Fact.Description: True when /form7206PlanEstablishingBusinessCount is exactly 1. It is the switch /form7206Line4NetProfitOfBusiness computes the attested business's own net profit behind, and the arm scheduleSE /knockoutSelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction NARROWS by and scheduleSE /selfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction (Schedule 1 line 17) computes behind on a multi-business return: those two facts must stay in lockstep, so a return this predicate admits is filed and never silently zero, and a return it does not admit is refused, never filed with the single-business figure. THREE COUNTING STATES, and only the middle one is admitted: a count of 0 is "nobody was asked, or every business said no", and /form7206Line4NetProfitOfBusiness falls back to the single-profitable-business reading it always had; a count of 1 is this predicate, and line 4 is the attested business's own figure; a count of 2 or more is the "more than one health plan and business" case the instructions send to separate Forms 7206, which this singleton module does not model and which stays refused.

Fact.Name: Form 7206 line 4 Schedule C term: the attested Schedule C business's own line 31
Fact.Description: The CollectionSum of /scheduleCs/*/form7206PlanBusinessNetProfit, guarded in the module's collection shape so a return with no Schedule C reads $0. With exactly one attested business the sum is that business's own line 31, signed.

Fact.Name: Form 7206 line 4 K-1 term: the attested partnership's box 14 code A earnings
Fact.Description: The CollectionSum of /formK1s/*/form7206PlanBusinessSeEarnings, guarded in the module's collection shape so a return with no K-1 reads $0. With exactly one attested business the sum is that partnership's declared box 14 code A figure, signed.

Fact.Name: Form 7206 line 4 computed: the attested plan business's own net profit
Fact.Description: The three per-source line 4 terms added: /form7206ScheduleCPlanBusinessNetProfit, /form7206K1PlanBusinessSeEarnings and /form7206ScheduleFPlanBusinessNetProfit. Read by /form7206Line4NetProfitOfBusiness only behind /form7206PlanEstablishingBusinessAttestedExactlyOne, where at most one term is nonzero and the sum is that one business's own figure, signed. NOT MODELLED, inherited from the shipping line 4 and named rather than dropped: the footnote's optional-method substitution ("If you used either optional method to figure your net earnings from self-employment from any business, don't enter your net profit from the business. Instead, enter the amount attributable to that business from Schedule SE (Form 1040), Part I, line 4b"), the "any other earned income" addend (gains on property the filer created) and the Conservation Reserve Program exclusion; each is a per-business figure no fact splits by business.

Fact.Name: Form 7206 line 5 Schedule C term: every profitable Schedule C business's line 31, losses dropped
Fact.Description: The CollectionSum of /scheduleCs/*/form7206ScheduleCProfitOnly, guarded in the module's collection shape so a return with no Schedule C reads $0. This is the printed line 5's Schedule C term as written, "the total of all net profits* from Schedule C (Form 1040), line 31 ... Don't include any net losses shown on these schedules": each business's own line 31 floored at zero before the total, where scheduleC /scheduleCNetProfit nets them. Identical to the net whenever no Schedule C shows a loss, which is every committed return that reaches this form.

Fact.Name: Form 7206 line 5 term: the oil or gas working interest's net profit, profit only
Fact.Description: scheduleE /workingInterestNetProfit floored at zero, and $0 when that fact is Incomplete. The working interest is the second Schedule C business scheduleC /scheduleCNetProfit combines at line 31 without a collection item of its own (its Description says so in terms), so the line 5 total must carry it as a profitable business exactly as it carries each Schedule C item, and the line 4 fallback must keep it for the same reason. IT CANNOT BE ATTESTED: no item exists to put the attestation on, so a plan established under the working-interest activity itself has no line 4 route; on a multi-business return that filer cannot reach an attestation count of 1 and stays refused, which is a named residue of this change.

Fact.Name: Form 7206 line 5 term: all profitable Schedule C businesses, the working interest included
Fact.Description: /form7206ScheduleCProfitsOnlyTotal plus /form7206WorkingInterestProfitOnly: every Schedule C line 31 that is a profit, plus the working interest when it is one. This is the Schedule C term of the printed line 5 and, when no business is attested, the fallback line 4 as well: on the single-profitable-business population scheduleSE /selfEmployedHealthInsuranceSingleProfitableBusiness admits (exactly one profitable Schedule C, no farm profit, no working-interest profit) it is exactly that one business's own line 31, which is what line 4 always claimed to be. It replaces scheduleC /scheduleCNetProfit in both places, and differs from it only when a Schedule C or the working interest shows a LOSS beside the profitable business, where the net understated line 4 by the loss (the plan business's own net profit is not reduced by another business's loss, section 162(l)(2)(A) measuring "the trade or business with respect to which the plan ... is established") and understated line 5 by the same loss (the printed line says not to include net losses). No committed return has that shape; the node fixture f7206-one-profit-one-loss-unattested-line-4-is-the-profitable-business pins the corrected figure.

Fact.Name: Months self-employed and not eligible for an employer-subsidised health plan
Fact.Description:
The set of 2025 calendar months in which the filer was self-employed AND was not eligible to participate in a health plan subsidised by an employer - the filer's own employer, the spouse's, or a dependent's. It is the month set Publication 974 calls the specified-premium months once it is intersected with the Form 1095-A coverage months.
SCREEN SPECIFICATION (this Description is the screen spec; the application builds the screen from it and does not open an IRS document).
QUESTION TEXT: "In which months of 2025 were you self-employed AND not eligible to participate in a health plan subsidised by an employer - yours, your spouse's, or a dependent's? Any part of a month counts as the whole month."
HELP TEXT: "Pick every month in which you were self-employed, even for part of the month - if you were self-employed for any part of a month, that whole month counts. But leave out any month in which you (or your spouse, or a dependent) could have joined a health plan an employer pays part of, whether or not you actually joined it. Being ELIGIBLE is what matters, not being enrolled." Source of the rule: IRC 162(l)(2)(B) (26 U.S.C. 162, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section162&num=0&edition=2024) and 2025 Publication 974 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p974.pdf, page 49 for the self-employed months and the part-month rule, lines 3020 to 3024 for the employer-plan exclusion as Worksheet P line 1 states it).
ASKED WHEN: the return carries a Marketplace qualified health plan and a self-employed health insurance deduction is in play - gated in the flow on ptc:/hasPtcQualifyingPlan AND scheduleSE:/writableSelfEmployedPaidHealthInsurancePremiums. It is NOT asked of a filer with no Form 1095-A, and it is NOT asked of a filer who paid no health insurance premiums.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: REFUSED, not defaulted. Every derived month fact below reads false when the set is unanswered (the IsComplete guard), which makes Worksheet W line 1 $0; the return is then carried out of the simplified method entirely by residual (vii) of scheduleSE:/pub974CoordinationResidual (a later sub-stage of this change) and refused, because a $0 specified-premium figure on a filer who did have specified premiums would silently understate Schedule 1 line 17. The false-on-unanswered posture exists so the graph stays complete, NOT so the return can be filed on it.
VALIDATION: multi-select of the twelve months of the tax year, options constants:/monthOptions with the printed labels January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, December.
ZERO MONTHS SELECTED. Zero selected months is accepted by the control and is DIFFERENT from leaving the question unanswered, but on BOTH Publication 974 populations it now leads to a REFUSAL rather than to a filed return, and the application should say so on the screen ("If no month of 2025 was both self-employed and free of employer-subsidised coverage, this return needs a preparer"). Why, on each population. (a) SIMPLIFIED METHOD: /pub974SimplifiedMethodApplies carries GreaterThanOrEqual(/pub974SpecifiedMonthCount, 1), so an empty set takes the return out of the method and it stays in knockout arm 4. (b) FALLBACK ROUTE: /pub974FallbackApplies carries the same conjunct. There, the filer has typed EVERY premium into Form 7206 line 1 after applying the employer-plan month exclusion themselves, so an empty month set here contradicts that figure; and if the empty set is the true answer then IRC 162(l)(2)(B) allows no deduction at all while the tree would file the whole typed figure. The tree cannot tell a deliberate zero from a click-through, so it refuses, and scheduleSE:/pub974CoordinationResidual member (xv) NAMES the refusal. Both postures are pinned: f7206-pub974-carla-answered-empty-month-set-is-refused and f7206-pub974-fallback-answered-empty-month-set-is-refused. (The publication's own point about a month that is not self-employed - p974 :3122-3134, such a premium is "neither" specified nor nonspecified - is unaffected; it is about which BUCKET a month falls in, not about whether the return can be filed when no month falls in either.) No month may be selected that the filer was not self-employed in; the screen may pre-fill from the business start and end dates but must let the filer change it.
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: /pub974Section162lMonth{Jan..Dec}, then /pub974SpecifiedMonth{Jan..Dec} (intersected with the Form 1095-A coverage months), /pub974SpecifiedMonthCount, and through those Worksheet W lines 1 and 2 - the specified premiums and the APTC attributable to them.

Fact.Name: The Marketplace policy also covers someone outside the coverage family
Fact.Description:
Whether the qualified health plan the Form 1095-A reports also covered at least one individual who is NOT in the filer's coverage family - typically a spouse or a child who could enrol in an employer plan of their own, or a tax-family member with other minimum essential coverage.
SCREEN SPECIFICATION (this Description is the screen spec).
QUESTION TEXT: "Did the Marketplace plan on your Form 1095-A also cover someone who is NOT part of your coverage family for the premium tax credit - for example a spouse or child who could have enrolled in a health plan through their own employer?"
HELP TEXT: "Your coverage family is the people in your tax family who were enrolled in the Marketplace plan and were not eligible for other minimum essential coverage - for example Medicare, Medicaid, or an employer plan. If the plan also covered someone outside that group, only part of the premium counts toward your self-employed health insurance deduction, and that part has to be worked out with the second lowest cost silver plan premiums for each group. Answer yes and we will tell you this return needs a preparer." Source of the rule: 2025 Publication 974 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p974.pdf, page 48, the portion of a qualified health plan premium "attributable to individuals not in your coverage family" is a NONSPECIFIED premium; lines 3146 to 3147 and 3086 to 3092, the SLCSP fraction that splits it).
ASKED WHEN: the return carries a Form 1095-A and the filer is claiming a self-employed health insurance deduction - the same gate as the month set above, asked immediately after it.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: REFUSED. An unanswered answer is residual (vii) of scheduleSE:/pub974CoordinationResidual (a later sub-stage), exactly as an unanswered month set is: this dictionary cannot tell whether the premium needs splitting, and guessing "no" would overstate the specified premiums for every filer whose plan covers a non-coverage-family member. Answered YES is residual (ii) and is ALSO refused, because the SLCSP allocation fraction the publication prescribes needs a per-person applicable-SLCSP premium this dictionary does not collect. Only an answered NO admits the return to the simplified method.
VALIDATION: Boolean, yes or no, no default.
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: nothing arithmetically - it is a pure admission gate. It is read by scheduleSE:/pub974CoordinationResidual (built in a later sub-stage of this change), whose true value routes the return to the existing self-employed-health-insurance refusal. It is recorded here, with the month set, because the two questions belong on one screen and because the specified-premium definition they jointly implement is one rule.
FOLLOW-UP NAMED, NOT BUILT: a per-person coverage-family and applicable-SLCSP intake would let the allocation fraction be computed and would free the YES population. It is queued as a named successor, not built here.

Fact.Name: January is a specified-premium month
Fact.Description:
Whether January 2025 is a month whose Marketplace enrollment premium is a SPECIFIED premium: a section 162(l) month (self-employed, no subsidised employer plan available) that is also a coverage month on a Form 1095-A the return carries.
WHY THE COVERAGE-MONTH CONJUNCT. A premium is a SPECIFIED premium only for a month that is a coverage month on the Form 1095-A - p974 :3113-3118 defines a specified qualified health plan as one covering a member of the coverage family "for a month for which your enrollment premium(s) has been paid by the due date". A month the filer was self-employed and enrolled in but which is NOT a coverage month is a NONSPECIFIED premium month (p974 :3074-3075, "Premiums paid for a qualified health plan other than during a coverage month"), and this dictionary does not compute that slice: it is residual (ix) of scheduleSE:/pub974CoordinationResidual and is refused, so no premium is silently dropped.
COMPLETENESS. The section 162(l) conjunct is FIRST and is complete-safe to false, so on an unanswered month set the All resolves Complete false whatever the policy leg does (an All is Complete false as soon as any conjunct is Complete false). On a return whose month set IS answered but whose Form 1095-A is not yet complete, the policy leg is Incomplete and so is this fact - that is the data-completeness residue residual (vii) refuses, and it is deliberately not defaulted away.
