Fact.Name: Number of specified-premium months
Fact.Description: How many of the twelve months of 2025 are specified-premium months. It is the numerator of the annual-route apportionment on Worksheet W lines 1 and 2: when the Form 1095-A reports annual totals rather than twelve monthly figures, the share of the annual premium that is a specified premium is that annual figure times this count over twelve. Zero is a legitimate value and means no premium on the return is a specified premium.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 Worksheet W line 1: specified premiums
Fact.Description:
Worksheet W line 1: the SPECIFIED premiums - the Marketplace enrollment premiums for the months that are both section 162(l) months and Form 1095-A coverage months. It is the figure Publication 974's Simplified Calculation Method limits the self-employed health insurance deduction to, and it is also Worksheet X line 27.
TWO ROUTES, BECAUSE THE FORM 1095-A HAS TWO. When every policy on the return qualifies to report ANNUAL totals (ptc:/ptcCanReportAnnualTotals - a full-year policy with no change in premium or SLCSP, or a zero-coverage-month policy with APTC), the Form 1095-A carries one annual enrollment premium and no monthly column, so the specified share is that annual figure apportioned by months: annual x specified months / 12, rounded once. Otherwise the monthly columns exist and the specified premiums are their sum over the specified months. Both routes read only item-level and return-level premium facts that stage 0b measured clean of /potentiallyApplicableTaxPayer.
WHY THE ANNUAL ROUTE IS NOT "TWELVE MONTHLY TWELFTHS ADDED UP". ptc:/1095As/*/ptcMonthlyPremium{M} falls back to annual / 12 when the annual route is live, and twelve of those added back gives 12 x 1,083.33 = 12,999.96 on a $13,000 annual premium, not $13,000. The publication apportions the ANNUAL figure (Carla's Worksheet W line 1 is exactly 13,000 on a 13,000 annual premium and twelve specified months, p974 :3783-3784), so the annual route multiplies before it divides and rounds once at the end.
THE ANNUAL-ROUTE GUARD IS All(IsComplete(x), x), NOT a bare read. ptc:/ptcCanReportAnnualTotals is Incomplete on a return whose Form 1095-A is unanswered, and a Switch case whose When resolves Incomplete downgrades every LATER case to a Placeholder (Expression.switches.resultRecurse, the engine fact stage 0b measured). Wrapping it makes the When always Complete, so the monthly route below it resolves normally.
COMPLETE-SAFE TO $0. With no Form 1095-A, or with the month set unanswered, every /pub974SpecifiedMonth{M} is Complete false, the annual guard is Complete false, and the twelve monthly terms each take their $0 default. That $0 is a graph-completeness value and NOT a filing position: residual (vii) of scheduleSE:/pub974CoordinationResidual takes the unanswered return out of the method.
NOT MODELLED, NAMED HERE. The coverage-family allocation fraction (p974 :3086-3092) - a policy covering someone outside the coverage family is refused through /writablePub974PolicyCoversNonCoverageFamilyMember, so line 1 never has to prorate. The other-tax-family allocation (p974 :3136-3144, Form 8962 Part IV) is refused through ptc:/needsAllocations. A month the filer was self-employed and enrolled in that is NOT a coverage month is residual (ix) and refused rather than added here.
THE ANNUAL ROUTE ASSUMES ONE POLICY, AND THAT IS residual (iii), NOT AN APPROXIMATION LEFT LYING ABOUT. ptc:/totalPtcAnnualPremium sums EVERY policy's annual premium while /pub974SpecifiedMonthCount is a single return-level count, so on a return carrying two policies with different coverage-month sets - say one full-year policy beside a zero-coverage-month policy with APTC, which ptc:/ptcCanReportAnnualTotals admits - the count would come from one policy and the premium from both, and line 1 would OVERSTATE. That population is refused outright by residual (iii) (ptc:/hasMultiple1095As), so no return can reach the overstatement; it is named here so a later author who narrows residual (iii) knows this line must be re-derived per policy first. The MONTHLY route has no such dependence: each month's CollectionSum is taken only for the months the return itself calls specified, whatever the policy count.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 Worksheet W line 2: APTC attributable to the specified premiums
Fact.Description:
Worksheet W line 2: the advance payments of the premium tax credit shown in Form 1095-A Part III column C that are ATTRIBUTABLE to the line 1 specified premiums - the APTC for the specified months. Line 3 subtracts it from line 1, so what line 3 carries is the specified premiums the filer actually bore.
Same two routes and the same guard shape as line 1, over ptc:/totalAnnualAptcAmount and ptc:/1095As/*/ptcMonthlyAptcPremium{M}; see line 1's Description for why the annual route multiplies before it divides, and for the All(IsComplete(x), x) guard. Complete-safe to $0 on the same populations.
LINE 2 IS ALSO THE WORKSHEET'S OWN ROUTE SWITCH. Line 18 asks whether line 2 is blank or -0-; if it is, Worksheet X is skipped entirely and the filer uses one of the methods that follow it (p974 :3186-3188). That is why this line exists as its own fact even though line 3 could have been written directly off the premium and APTC totals.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 Worksheet W line 3: specified premiums less the attributable APTC
Fact.Description:
Worksheet W line 3, line 1 less line 2: the specified premiums net of the advance credit paid on them. It is the first of the two figures line 16 takes the smaller of - the deduction for specified premiums can never exceed the premiums the filer actually bore after the advance credit, which is the sum rule Publication 974 states at :2988-2993 ("you may use any computation method that results in reporting amounts that satisfy the rules for both the deduction and PTC, as long as the sum of the deduction claimed for the premiums and the PTC computed, taking the deduction into account, is less than or equal to the enrollment premiums").
SIGNED, NOT FLOORED. The publication says plainly "Subtract line 2 from line 1" and both the deduction and the credit are bounded by the enrollment premium, so line 2 cannot exceed line 1 on a correct Form 1095-A; a negative here would mean the reported APTC exceeded the reported enrollment premium, which is a Form 1095-A defect and not something to hide behind a floor.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 Worksheet W line 15: earned income limit left after the nonspecified deduction
Fact.Description:
Worksheet W line 15, line 13 less line 14: how much of the section 162(l)(2)(A) earned income ceiling is still unused after the deduction for NONSPECIFIED premiums has taken its share.
LINES 4 TO 14 ARE THE SHIPPING FORM 7206 LINES, NOT TWINS. Worksheet W lines 4 to 13 are word for word Form 7206 lines 4 to 13, and line 14 is "your self-employed health insurance deduction for nonspecified premiums from Worksheet P, line 3, or Form 7206, line 14" - the publication itself sends the filer to the form. So this fact reads /form7206Line13EarnedIncomeLimit and /form7206Line14SelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction directly and NO Worksheet W twin of lines 4 to 14 is minted. The Worksheet W caution (p974 :3152-3154) says lines 4 to 13 are completed separately for each trade or business under which a qualified health plan is established and their line 13s added; the simplified method is admitted only for a return with exactly ONE such business (form7206:/form7206PlanEstablishingBusinessAttestedExactlyOne or scheduleSE:/selfEmployedHealthInsuranceSingleProfitableBusiness), so the sum over businesses is the single business's own line 13 and the reuse is exact.
WHAT MAKES FORM 7206 LINE 14 THE NONSPECIFIED FIGURE. Form 7206 line 1 is scheduleSE:/writableSelfEmployedHealthInsurancePremiumsPaid. On a return in the simplified method that intake means the NONSPECIFIED premiums only - the Marketplace premiums for the coverage months are handled with the credit and must not be entered there.
NOT FLOORED AT $0. The publication says "Subtract line 14 from line 13". Line 14 is already floored at $0 and is the smaller of Form 7206 line 3 and line 13, so line 15 is negative only when line 13 itself is - a plan business with a loss, or a Schedule 1 line 16 deduction larger than the business's profit net of the SE-tax share. Line 16 then takes the smaller of a negative line 15 and line 3 and the negative propagates; the Schedule 1 line 17 arm that consumes line 17 floors it, exactly as form7206:/form7206Line14SelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction is floored, and THAT floor is where the sign is settled - not here, where the worksheet's own arithmetic must be reproducible line by line.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 Worksheet W line 16: the deduction allowed for specified premiums
Fact.Description:
Worksheet W line 16, the smaller of line 3 and line 15: the deduction the filer may take for SPECIFIED premiums. Two ceilings meet here - the premiums actually borne after the advance credit (line 3, the IRC 36B sum rule) and the earned income still unused after the nonspecified deduction (line 15, the IRC 162(l)(2)(A) ceiling).
THIS IS A LIMIT, NOT THE FINAL FIGURE. On a return that goes on to Worksheet X the credit is recomputed at the interim deduction and line 16 is superseded by the Step 3 result; line 16 is the figure the filer uses only when line 2 is blank or -0- and Worksheet X is skipped (p974 :3186-3188). Its consumers are Worksheet W line 17 and line 19.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 Worksheet W line 17: total self-employed health insurance deduction limit
Fact.Description:
Worksheet W line 17, line 14 plus line 16: the whole self-employed health insurance deduction the simplified method allows - the nonspecified part plus the specified part.
WHERE IT GOES. p974 :3486-3488: if the filer did not have to fill out Worksheet X, line 17 IS the Schedule 1 line 17 figure; if Worksheet X was completed, Worksheet X line 31 supersedes it. The Schedule 1 line 17 arm that chooses between them is a later sub-stage of this change; nothing reads this fact yet, which is why it carries Export downstreamFacts.
THE FLOOR IS THE CONSUMER'S. See line 15's Description: line 17 can be negative only where line 13 is, and the Schedule 1 line 17 arm floors it at $0 the way form7206:/form7206Line14SelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction is floored.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 Worksheet W line 18: is line 2 blank or -0-
Fact.Description:
Worksheet W line 18, the worksheet's own route switch: "Is line 2 blank or -0-?" TRUE (the printed Yes) means no advance credit is attributable to the specified premiums, line 19 and Worksheet X are both skipped, and the filer uses one of the methods that follow Worksheet X. FALSE (the printed No) sends the filer to line 19 and on to Worksheet X.
BLANK AND -0- ARE THE SAME VALUE HERE. Line 2 is complete-safe to $0 in this dictionary - a return with no Form 1095-A, no APTC, or no specified month resolves it to $0 rather than leaving it unresolved - so "blank or -0-" is exactly Equal(line 2, $0). Negative is impossible: advance payments are non-negative.
THE WORKSHEET X SELECTOR IS NOT THIS FACT. Worksheet X is completed "only if APTC was paid to your insurer on your behalf for the months you were self-employed" (p974 :3199-3200), which is what line 18 tests, but the selector fact form7206:/pub974WorksheetXApplies also carries the admission conditions for the method as a whole and is built in a later sub-stage.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 Worksheet W line 19: earned income limit still unused
Fact.Description:
Worksheet W line 19, line 15 less line 16: how much of the earned income ceiling is STILL unused after the line 16 deduction for specified premiums. Worksheet X lines 15, 19 and 22 cap the extra deduction the recomputed credit allows at the smaller of this figure and a printed dollar amount, so line 19 is the headroom the second pass may spend.
SKIPPED IS ENCODED AS $0. The printed worksheet skips line 19 when line 18 is Yes, and a return that skips line 19 also skips Worksheet X, so nothing downstream can read the value. Encoding the skip as $0 rather than leaving it unresolved keeps every consumer complete-safe and cannot leak: the only readers are Worksheet X lines 15, 19 and 22, and form7206:/pub974WorksheetXApplies is false on exactly the population line 18 sends away.

Fact.Name: The only Schedule E activity on the return is an investment royalty
Fact.Description: True when the return claims Schedule E royalty income and no other Schedule E intake: no rental real estate, no partnership or S corporation Schedule K-1, no estate or trust Schedule K-1, no REMIC residual interest and no Form 4835 farm rental. These are the six intakes scheduleE:/scheduleEActivityPresent lists. On that return Schedule E line 41 is the royalty net alone, and royalty property is not a passive activity, so the figure never reaches the section 8582 modified adjusted gross income and cannot depend on the self-employed health insurance deduction. That makes the royalty the one Schedule E slice Publication 974 Worksheet X line 1 can carry exactly: /pub974WorksheetXLine1TotalIncomeAndTaxExemptInterest adds scheduleE:/royaltyNetIncome on this population. It is built to be read by the Schedule E member of scheduleSE:/pub974CoordinationResidual, whose bare Schedule E test still refuses this return until that member reads it. Every intake gate read here is complete-safe false when unanswered, so this fact is Complete on every return.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 Worksheet X line 1: total income plus tax-exempt interest
Fact.Description:
Worksheet X line 1, "Combine the amounts from Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, lines 2a, 9, and the excess, if any, of line 6a over line 6b" - Form 1040 total income, plus tax-exempt interest, plus the untaxed part of social security benefits. It is the modified-AGI base the whole of Worksheet X Part I works down from, and it is deliberately built WITHOUT any Schedule 1 adjustment so that no term of it can depend on the self-employed health insurance deduction the method is solving for.
LINE 9 IS THE BOUND, AND THE BOUND IS EXACT ON THE ADMITTED POPULATION. The obvious operand, income:/totalIncome, is unusable: it reaches taxCalculations:/adjustmentsExcludingStudentLoanAndIra through /taxableSocialSecurityBenefits, so a Worksheet X built on it would close a resolution cycle through the very deduction it computes. income:/totalIncomeUpperBoundForIraMagi (income.xml:4820) is the SAME thirteen-addend total with the three AGI-dependent addends replaced by upper bounds and /scheduleETotalIncome omitted, and it is measured free of that cycle. It is a DOMINANCE BOUND in general and an IDENTITY exactly where its three substitutions are identities and its one omission is empty: no social security benefits, no IRA distributions and no Form 8606/8915-F amount, no employer adoption benefits, and no Schedule E activity. Every one of those four populations is REFUSED by the method's residual - (x), (xi), (xii) and (xiii) of the residual fact scheduleSE:/pub974CoordinationResidual - so on the population that reaches this worksheet line 1 IS Form 1040 line 9, exactly. That equality is not left as prose: every fixture of this change asserts /pub974WorksheetXLine1TotalIncomeAndTaxExemptInterest against income:/totalIncome, and on a refusal fixture the row records the difference as the reason the return is refused. The bound carries two PRE-EXISTING undischarged obligations of its own (income.xml:4826-4835: the Schedule F classification row in scripts/ira_magi_bound_addends.tsv and the Schedule SE benefits-worksheet line 3 mirror); this change adds a consumer to that bound and adds no addend to it, and its addend set must never be widened from here.
THE 6a-OVER-6b TERM IS $0 BY REFUSAL, NOT BY OMISSION. socialSecurity:/nonTaxableSocialSecurityBenefits is itself on the AGI cycle, and the population that has any is refused by residual (x) (socialSecurity:/hasSocialSecurityBenefits), so the term is identically zero wherever this fact is read and is not written. The Form 2555 term of line 2 is $0 the same way (form2555:/knockoutFilesForm2555, residual (vi)), which is why line 3 ("Add lines 1 and 2") is not a fact of its own: line 3 IS line 1 on every return the method admits, and ptc:/ptcMagi omits the same Form 2555 term for the same reason (ptc.xml:2036).
FORM 8814 IS THE ONE DISCLOSED NARROWING. The line 1 instruction adds a Form 8814 child's tax-exempt interest, the lesser of Form 8814 line 4 or line 5, and the child's nontaxable social security when Form 8814 line 4 exceeds $1,350. This fact does not, mirroring exactly what the shipping ptc:/ptcMagi already does not do (ptc.xml:2014-2037 adds only AGI, tax-exempt interest and nontaxable social security). Modelling it here and not there would make the method's household income and the shipping Form 8962 household income disagree on the same return, which is worse than the disclosed narrowing.
THE ROYALTY SLICE IS BUILT; THE K-1 SLICE IS NOT. On a return whose only Schedule E intake is an investment royalty (/pub974ScheduleERoyaltyOnly), line 1 adds scheduleE:/royaltyNetIncome, which is clean of the deduction, and the X1 == /totalIncome identity is pinned on a royalty-only fixture. That return is still refused by residual (xiii), whose bare Schedule E test does not yet read the detector. The nonpassive partnership K-1 slice is not built: scheduleE:/k1NonpassiveActiveNet is not Schedule E line 32 (it is figured before section 179 and leaves out guaranteed payments), so the identity cannot hold on it; every other Schedule E population omits /scheduleETotalIncome here and stays refused.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 Worksheet X line 8: the taxpayer's modified AGI at the interim deduction
Fact.Description:
Worksheet X line 8, line 3 less line 7: the TAXPAYER's modified AGI computed with the self-employed health insurance deduction set to Worksheet W line 14 plus Worksheet W line 16, rather than to the figure Schedule 1 line 17 will eventually carry. This is the whole point of Worksheet X Part I - a modified AGI at a KNOWN deduction, so that the repayment limitation Part III computes is not circular.
THE THREE PRINTED LINES THIS FACT FOLDS. Line 7 is "Add lines 4, 5, and 6" and line 8 is "Subtract line 7 from line 3"; neither line 7 nor line 3 has a consumer other than line 8, and line 2 is $0 by refusal (see line 1's Description), so this single Subtract is lines 3, 7 and 8 together with one rounding boundary rather than three. Line 4, line 5 and line 6 are each read from the fact that already holds them: - LINE 4 IS taxCalculations:/adjustmentsExcludingStudentLoanIraAndSelfEmployedHealthInsurance, NOT A TWIN. That fact exists FOR this line, and says so in its own Description: it is the Schedule 1 Part II adjustments Add with the line 17 term lifted out, and the IRA (line 20) and student loan interest (line 21) terms already outside it. One quantity, one fact - no Worksheet X line 4 fact is minted. - LINE 5 IS Worksheet W line 14, which is Form 7206 line 14 (/form7206Line14SelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction), by the worksheet's own instruction. - LINE 6 IS /pub974WorksheetWLine16SpecifiedPremiumDeduction.
TWO DISCLOSED DIVERGENCES FROM THE PRINTED LINE 4, BOTH DELIBERATE. (1) BROADER: the printed enumeration is "Schedule 1 (Form 1040), lines 11 through 16, 18, and 19a, plus any write-in adjustments you entered on the dotted line next to Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 26". The subtotal this fact reads ALSO carries Schedule 1 line 23 (the Archer MSA deduction) and Schedule 1 line 25 (the total of the line 24a-24z other adjustments). That is the correct reading, not an over-count: line 8 must be a modified AGI, and a modified AGI subtracts every above-the-line deduction except the three the method is holding constant or has refused. The printed list is the pre-2018 Form 1040 page-1 adjustment block carried forward; the "write-in adjustments on the dotted line next to line 26" clause is that block's own catch-all and lines 23 and 25 are what it became. Both terms are complete-safe $0 on every return that does not answer them, so the divergence is invisible except on a return that has an Archer MSA or a line 24 adjustment, and including them keeps line 8 equal to the AGI-based modified AGI the Form 8962 chain computes. (2) NARROWER: no IRA deduction term. The printed note is "Include your IRA deduction on line 4 only if you (and your spouse if filing a joint return) were not covered by a retirement plan at work or through self-employment." The covered case is refused by the special-instructions residual (i) and the NOT-covered case is refused by residual (xiv), because the shipping iraDeduction:/primaryFilerPlainTraditionalIraDeduction is itself on the AGI cycle (/iraDeductionLimitFromPhaseout -> /iraDeductionMagiExcess -> /magiForIraDeduction) and an un-phased twin of it on the not-covered sub-population is the class one-quantity-one-fact refuses. So on every return this fact is read on, the IRA term is zero because the filer made no traditional IRA contribution - plan v2 BLOCKER 3, decision (i).
NOT FLOORED. The publication says "Subtract line 7 from line 3" with no floor, and unlike lines 16, 20 and 23 it prints no "If zero or less, enter -0-". A negative line 8 is a filer whose adjustments exceed their total income, whose household income is then below 100% of the poverty line and who is refused by the knockout-only residual scheduleSE:/pub974CannotTakePtcStop, so flooring here would only hide the input to that refusal.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 Worksheet X line 14: household income at the interim deduction
Fact.Description:
Worksheet X line 14, "Household income. Add lines 8 and 13": the taxpayer's modified AGI at the Worksheet W line 14 plus line 16 deduction, plus the combined modified AGI of the dependents in the tax family who were required to file. It is the household income Part III of Worksheet X measures against the poverty line to pick the repayment limitation, and it is NOT ptc:/householdIncome - that fact is built on the final AGI, which is built on the deduction this whole method is still solving for.
PART II IS ptc:/ptcDependentsModifiedAgiOrZero, NOT A TWIN. Worksheet X lines 9 to 13 are the dependents' combined AGI, their tax-exempt interest, their Form 2555 amounts and their untaxed social security - which is Form 8962 line 2b, and this dictionary collects that as one intake, ptc:/writablePtcDependentsModifiedAgi, read through its complete-safe wrapper ptc:/ptcDependentsModifiedAgiOrZero. Lines 9 to 13 are therefore that one fact and no Worksheet X twin of them is minted; a filer with no dependents required to file skips Part II and the wrapper gives the $0 the printed worksheet's skip gives. The wrapper's $0 default is also what makes this fact complete-safe on a return that never answers the dependents' MAGI question.
THE DEPENDENTS' TERM IS THE SAME IN BOTH PASSES. Nothing about a dependent's own modified AGI depends on this filer's self-employed health insurance deduction, so the interim household income and the final household income use the identical line 2b figure. That is why Part II needs no interim twin while Part I does.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 Worksheet X line 16: household income less the under-200% repayment cap
Fact.Description:
Worksheet X line 16, "Subtract line 15 from line 14. If zero or less, enter -0-". Line 15 is "the smaller of Worksheet W, line 19, or $750 ($375 if your filing status is single)" and is folded into this fact rather than minted, because line 15 has no other consumer.
WHAT PART III IS DOING, SO THE THREE ROUNDS READ AS ONE THING. The repayment limitation is a function of household income as a percent of the poverty line, and household income here is a function of the deduction - so the worksheet solves the fixed point by TRYING the bands from the bottom. It provisionally allows the smallest cap ($750), asks what percent of the poverty line the household income would then be (line 18), and if that lands under 200% the $750 cap is consistent with itself and is the answer. If not, it tries $1,950 (lines 19-21), then $3,250 (lines 22-24). Each subtraction is the SAME line 14, never the previous line's result - lines 20 and 23 both say "Subtract line 19 [22] from line 14" - so the three attempts are independent trials, not a cascade, and each of the three is the household income the filer would have if that band's extra deduction were allowed.
THE $750/$375 PAIR IS THE SHIPPING PARAMETER, NOT A LITERAL. The two amounts are the IRC 36B(f)(2)(B) excess-APTC repayment caps for household income under 200% of the poverty line, and they are already carried as ptc:/ptcRepaymentLimitationLessThan200PercentFplOther ($750) and ptc:/ptcRepaymentLimitationLessThan400PercentFplSingle's siblings - here ptc:/ptcRepaymentLimitationLessThan200PercentFplSingle ($375), both with their own param: ledger annotations and their own Rev. Proc. authority. No new Dollar literal is minted for them. The single/other split is filingStatus:/isFilingStatusSingle, copied verbatim from the shipping ptc:/ptcRepaymentLimitation, so head of household and the other statuses take the full cap exactly as they do on Form 8962 line 28.
THE FLOOR IS PRINTED. "If zero or less, enter -0-" is a GreaterOf against $0, the same floor idiom Form 7206 line 14 uses. It matters: line 16 divides the poverty line at line 18, and a negative numerator would produce a negative percent that compares below 200 and would wrongly select the smallest cap for a filer with no income at all.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 Worksheet X line 18: line 16 as a truncated percent of the poverty line
Fact.Description:
Worksheet X line 18, "Divide line 16 by line 17b" and express the result as a whole percent by TRUNCATION: "If the result is not a whole percentage, do not round; instead, multiply this number by 100 (to express it as a percentage) and then drop any numbers after the decimal point. For example, for 0.9984, enter the result as 99; for 1.8565, enter the result as 185; and for 3.997, enter the result as 399." Under 200 selects the $750/$375 cap and skips lines 19 through 24; 200 or more goes on to line 19.
LINE 17a AND 17b ARE THE SHIPPING FACTS. Line 17a is "the number of qualifying individuals in your tax family (including yourself)" = ptc:/taxFamilySize; line 17b is the poverty line for that size and the filer's state = ptc:/federalPovertyLevelThreshold, read here through its Rational sibling ptc:/federalPovertyLevelThresholdAsARational. Neither is twinned - family size and the poverty line do not depend on the deduction, so both passes use the same figures.
THE TRUNCATION IDIOM IS ptc:/householdIncomeAsPercent's, COPIED DELIBERATELY. Form 8962 line 5 states the identical instruction and ptc:/householdIncomeAsPercent (ptc.xml:2165) implements it as TruncateCents(numerator x 100 / denominator) -> x $1 -> StepwiseMultiply at rate 1/1 -> RoundToInt. The load-bearing step is the StepwiseMultiply: its operator is Dollar(x.intValue / denominator * numerator), and Dollar.intValue TRUNCATES toward zero, so a rate of 1/1 is exactly "drop the cents" - which is what makes 99.84 come out 99 rather than the 100 a rounding would give. Only after that does RoundToInt convert an already-integral Dollar to an Int. Re-deriving this in any other shape would silently round.
ONE DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE FROM THE SHIPPING FACT: NO 401 SHORTCUT. ptc:/householdIncomeAsPercent answers Int 401 whenever household income exceeds four times the poverty line, because Form 8962 line 5 only ever needs to know "over 400". Worksheet X asks a different question three times over against three different numerators, and lines 18 and 21 must be comparable to 200 and 300 as well; a return can be over 400% on line 18's numerator and under it on line 24's. So this fact computes the real truncated percent and takes no shortcut, and a fixture pins the printed 320/316/312 sequence rather than 401. The tax-family-size-zero guard IS kept, because it is the divide-by-zero guard: ptc:/federalPovertyLevelThreshold is $0 exactly when ptc:/taxFamilySizeIsZero is true.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 Worksheet X line 20: household income less the under-300% repayment cap
Fact.Description:
Worksheet X line 20, "Subtract line 19 from line 14. If zero or less, enter -0-", where line 19 is "the smaller of Worksheet W, line 19, or $1,950 ($975 if your filing status is single)". The SECOND trial of the Part III fixed point (see line 16's Description): the same household income less the next band's cap. Line 19 is folded in, having no other consumer, and the caps are the shipping ptc:/ptcRepaymentLimitationLessThan300PercentFpl{Single,Other} parameter facts.
REACHED, NOT ALWAYS COMPUTED. The printed worksheet skips lines 19 through 24 when line 18 is under 200. This fact does not carry that skip, and deliberately: line 25 is the only consumer of the chain and it asks line 18 first, so a line 20 computed on a return that skipped it is never read. Encoding the skip here instead would need an Incomplete or a sentinel, and both are worse than an unread number. The same reasoning governs lines 21, 22, 23 and 24.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 Worksheet X line 21: line 20 as a truncated percent of the poverty line
Fact.Description: Worksheet X line 21, the same truncated-percent computation as line 18 over line 20's numerator: under 300 selects the $1,950/$975 cap and skips lines 22 through 24; 300 or more goes on to line 22. The truncation idiom, the tax-family-size-zero divide-by-zero guard and the reason no 401 shortcut is taken are all as stated on /pub974WorksheetXLine18PercentAfterFirstCap.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 Worksheet X line 23: household income less the under-400% repayment cap
Fact.Description: Worksheet X line 23, "Subtract line 22 from line 14. If zero or less, enter -0-", where line 22 is "the smaller of Worksheet W, line 19, or $3,250 ($1,625 if your filing status is single)". The THIRD and last trial of the Part III fixed point (see line 16's Description). Line 22 is folded in and the caps are the shipping ptc:/ptcRepaymentLimitationLessThan400PercentFpl{Single,Other} parameter facts. Whether it is reached is line 25's business, per line 20's Description.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 Worksheet X line 24: line 23 as a truncated percent of the poverty line
Fact.Description:
Worksheet X line 24, the same truncated-percent computation as lines 18 and 21 over line 23's numerator: under 400 selects the $3,250/$1,625 cap; 400 or more sends Worksheet W line 2 to line 25 instead of a cap. The truncation idiom, the divide-by-zero guard and the no-401-shortcut argument are on /pub974WorksheetXLine18PercentAfterFirstCap.
THIS IS THE LINE THAT DECIDES WHETHER THE CAP IS A CAP AT ALL. At 400 percent or more the filer has to repay every dollar of advance credit attributable to the specified premiums, so line 25 becomes Worksheet W line 2 - the attributable APTC itself - and the "limitation" stops limiting. That is the same cliff IRC 36B(f)(2)(B) draws, where the dollar bands simply do not apply at or above 400 percent of the poverty line.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 Worksheet X line 25: the repayment limitation for the simplified method
Fact.Description:
Worksheet X line 25, "Enter the amount you were instructed to enter here by line 18, 21, or 24". It is the excess-APTC repayment limitation computed at the METHOD's household income rather than at the return's final household income, and it is the quantity that makes the rest of Worksheet X work: the maximum deduction the method allows (line 26) is the specified-premium deduction already found plus whatever advance credit the filer would at worst have to repay.
THE FOUR ROUTES, IN THE PRINTED ORDER. Line 18 under 200 gives $750 ($375 single); otherwise line 21 under 300 gives $1,950 ($975); otherwise line 24 under 400 gives $3,250 ($1,625); otherwise (line 24 at 400 or more) the entry is Worksheet W line 2, the whole APTC attributable to the specified premiums, because at or above 400 percent of the poverty line IRC 36B(f)(2)(B) sets no limit at all. The Switch reproduces that order exactly, so the first band that qualifies wins and no later case can reach a return the printed worksheet told to stop.
WHY THIS IS A CASCADE OF Switch CASES AND NOT THREE INDEPENDENT TESTS. The printed instruction under line 18 is "Skip lines 19 through 24"; under line 21, "Skip lines 22 through 24". The skips matter only because the later lines would otherwise be computed on a filer who has no business computing them - and here they simply are not read, because a Switch stops at its first matching Case. The line 20, 21, 23 and 24 facts still resolve to numbers on such a return; those numbers have no consumer, which is stated on each of them.
THIS IS ALSO FORM 8962 LINE 28, ON THIS POPULATION. The printed instruction is "Also, enter this amount on line 28 of the Form 8962 you attach to your tax return if you are required to complete that line and you do not complete Worksheet Y. Do not enter an amount from Table 5 in the Form 8962 instructions." The arm that overrides ptc:/ptcRepaymentLimitation with this fact is a later sub-stage of this change, and it carries the "if you are required to complete that line" conjunct (the FINAL Form 8962 line 5 decides that, not this worksheet's line 24) and the "and you do not complete Worksheet Y" conjunct (satisfied by residual (i), which refuses every filer Worksheet Y exists for). Nothing reads this fact yet, which is why it carries Export downstreamFacts.
NO NEW DOLLAR LITERAL. All six band amounts are the shipping ptc:/ptcRepaymentLimitationLessThan{200,300,400}PercentFpl{Single,Other} parameter facts, each with its own Rev. Proc. 2024-40 authority and its own param: ledger annotation, and the single/other split is filingStatus:/isFilingStatusSingle exactly as ptc:/ptcRepaymentLimitation uses it.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 Worksheet X line 26: specified-premium deduction plus the repayment limitation
Fact.Description:
Worksheet X line 26, "Add lines 6 and 25": the Worksheet W line 16 deduction for specified premiums plus the repayment limitation from line 25. Part IV then trims it by the two ceilings that cannot be exceeded whatever the credit does - the specified premiums themselves (line 27 = Worksheet W line 1) and the earned income still available (line 29 = Worksheet W line 15).
WHY ADDING A REPAYMENT LIMITATION TO A DEDUCTION IS THE RIGHT ARITHMETIC. Worksheet W line 16 is the deduction allowed for specified premiums NET of the advance credit paid on them (line 3 is line 1 less line 2). If the filer ends up having to repay some of that advance credit, those repaid dollars were borne by the filer after all and become deductible premiums too. Line 25 is the most that can be repaid, so line 26 is the largest deduction the coordination could ever support, and lines 28 and 30 cut it back to what the premiums and the earned income allow.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 Worksheet X line 28: line 26 capped at the specified premiums
Fact.Description:
Worksheet X line 28, "Enter the smaller of line 26 or line 27", where line 27 is "the amount from Worksheet W, line 1" - the specified premiums themselves. Line 27 is read directly from /pub974WorksheetWLine1SpecifiedPremiums and no Worksheet X twin of it is minted; one quantity, one fact.
THE CEILING IS SECTION 162(l)(1) ITSELF. The deduction is "an amount equal to the amount paid during the taxable year for insurance"; no coordination with the credit can let the filer deduct more than the premiums that were paid. This is also the sum rule Publication 974 states at :2988-2993 in its other direction.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 Worksheet X line 30: line 28 capped at the remaining earned income
Fact.Description:
Worksheet X line 30, "Enter the smaller of line 28 or line 29", where line 29 is "the amount from Worksheet W, line 15" - the section 162(l)(2)(A) earned income ceiling left after the deduction for NONSPECIFIED premiums has taken its share. Line 29 is read directly from /pub974WorksheetWLine15EarnedIncomeLimitNetOfNonspecified and is not twinned.
NOTE WHICH WORKSHEET W LINE THIS IS. Line 29 is Worksheet W line 15, not line 19: the whole remaining earned income, not the part left over after line 16. That is deliberate in the printed worksheet - the line 16 deduction is INSIDE line 26 through line 6, so measuring line 26 against line 19 would subtract it twice. Lines 15, 19 and 22 of Worksheet X use line 19 because they are capping the EXTRA deduction the recomputed credit buys; line 29 is capping the total.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 Worksheet X line 31: the deduction the interim Form 8962 pass is figured at
Fact.Description:
Worksheet X line 31, "Add lines 5 and 30" - Worksheet W line 14 (the nonspecified deduction, which is Form 7206 line 14) plus line 30. It is the MAXIMUM self-employed health insurance deduction the coordination could support, and it is what Step 1 of the simplified calculation method uses as the deduction when it figures AGI, modified AGI and household income for the interim Form 8962 pass.
IT IS NOT THE DEDUCTION THAT GOES ON SCHEDULE 1. The printed worksheet is explicit that Carla "does not enter $12,050 on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 17" (p974 :3826-3827). Line 31 is an input to Step 1 and nothing else; the figure Schedule 1 line 17 finally carries is Step 3 line 11 (or the iterative method's deduction), which is smaller whenever the recomputed credit covers part of the premiums. Nothing may read this fact as a deduction.
SKIPPING WORKSHEET X IS NOT ENCODED HERE. A return whose Worksheet W line 18 is Yes skips Worksheet X entirely and uses Worksheet W line 17 as Step 1's deduction. That choice lives in /pub974Step1SelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction, one fact downstream, so that this fact stays the plain arithmetic of the printed line.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 simplified method Step 1: the deduction the interim pass is figured at
Fact.Description:
Step 1 of the Simplified Calculation Method: "Figure your AGI, modified AGI, and household income using Worksheet X, line 31, as your self-employed health insurance deduction. If you did not fill out Worksheet X, use the amount from Worksheet W, line 17."
THE ROUTE SWITCH IS WORKSHEET W LINE 18, NOT THE METHOD SELECTOR. Worksheet W line 18 is the publication's own test for whether Worksheet X is filled out: "Is line 2 blank or -0-? Yes. Skip line 19 and Worksheet X" (p974 :3185-3188), which is the same population as Worksheet X's own heading, "Complete this worksheet only if APTC was paid to your insurer on your behalf for the months you were self-employed" (:3199-3200). So this fact reads /pub974WorksheetWLine18NoAttributableAptc and nothing else. It deliberately does NOT read the method selector: whether the simplified method applies at all gates the CONSUMER - the Schedule 1 line 17 arm and the interim pass, both later sub-stages - not this fact, which must stay complete-safe and computable on any return so that the selector itself can be evaluated without circularity.
COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION. Line 18 is Equal(Worksheet W line 2, $0) over a complete-safe $0 default, so it is always Complete true or false and neither arm can be Incomplete: a return with no policy and no specified month takes the Yes route and gets Worksheet W line 17, which on such a return is Form 7206 line 14 plus $0 - the ordinary deduction.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 simplified method Step 1: household income at the interim deduction
Fact.Description:
Step 1's household income - the figure the INTERIM Form 8962 pass of Step 2 uses on its lines 3 and 5. It is Worksheet X's own household income arithmetic with one operand replaced: Worksheet X line 14 is built at the Worksheet W line 14 plus line 16 deduction (X lines 5 and 6), and Step 1 is built at /pub974Step1SelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction, which on the Worksheet X route is line 31 and on the skip route is Worksheet W line 17.
THE SHAPE, TERM BY TERM. Modified AGI is AGI plus tax-exempt interest plus untaxed social security (IRC 36B(d)(2)(B)), AGI is total income less the Schedule 1 Part II adjustments, and household income is that plus the dependents' modified AGI (IRC 36B(d)(2)(A)). So it is /pub974WorksheetXLine1TotalIncomeAndTaxExemptInterest (total income plus tax-exempt interest, the social security term $0 by refusal) less taxCalculations:/adjustmentsExcludingStudentLoanIraAndSelfEmployedHealthInsurance (every above-the-line deduction except the three the method holds constant or refuses) less the Step 1 deduction, plus ptc:/ptcDependentsModifiedAgiOrZero. Every divergence from the printed enumerations - the Schedule 1 line 23 and 25 terms carried, the IRA term dropped, the Form 8814 child items omitted, the Form 2555 term $0 - is stated once on /pub974WorksheetXLine1TotalIncomeAndTaxExemptInterest and /pub974WorksheetXLine8TaxpayerModifiedAgi and is identical here.
THIS IS NOT ptc:/householdIncome AND MUST NOT BE CONFUSED WITH IT. ptc:/householdIncome is built on taxCalculations:/agi, which is built on scheduleSE:/selfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction - the quantity this whole method is solving for. The interim pass of Step 2 reads THIS fact instead, which is what breaks the cycle; the FINAL Form 8962 pass of Step 4 goes back to the shipping household income, because by then Schedule 1 line 17 carries Step 3 line 11 (or the iterative method's deduction) and the AGI is real. The Worksheet 1-1 and 1-2 references in Step 1 are the Form 8962 instructions' modified-AGI worksheets, which are the same IRC 36B(d)(2) arithmetic spelled out for a filer working by hand.
NO FLOOR. The publication prints none, and a household income below 100 percent of the poverty line is a real input to the knockout-only residual (the filer who cannot take the PTC and must stop), not something to clamp away.

Fact.Name: Number of section 162(l) months the filer was enrolled in a Marketplace policy
Fact.Description:
How many of the twelve months of 2025 are BOTH a section 162(l) month (self-employed, no subsidised employer plan available) AND a month in which at least one Form 1095-A policy on the return was active. It exists only to be compared with /pub974SpecifiedMonthCount: a specified month is a 162(l) month that is a COVERAGE month, and a coverage month is narrower than an active month because it also requires that month's enrollment premium to have been paid by the due date (IRC 36B(c)(2)(A)). So this count is greater than the specified-month count exactly when the return carries a month the filer was self-employed and enrolled but which is not a coverage month, and Publication 974 calls the premium for such a month a NONSPECIFIED premium.
COMPLETENESS. This count is COMPLETE-SAFE. Each term is a Count over an All; a Count resolves an Incomplete operand to 0, so an Add of twelve Counts is Complete on EVERY return, including one whose Form 1095-A is missing or incomplete and one whose month set is unanswered - both simply give 0. It was MEASURED: on a return with no /1095As collection at all, and on a return whose coverage-month set is emptied so that every /pub974SpecifiedMonth{M} is Incomplete, this count and /pub974SpecifiedMonthCount both come back Complete 0. The consequence a later author must not undo: because a zero here is indistinguishable from "nothing was asked", Not(IsComplete(this fact)) can never be true and is dead as a detector. The data-completeness residue is carried instead by Not(IsComplete(/pub974WorksheetWLine1SpecifiedPremiums)) - which IS Incomplete when the Form 1095-A cannot resolve - and by member (xv), both in scheduleSE:/pub974CoordinationResidual. By the same Count semantics, /pub974SelfEmployedEnrolledNonCoverageMonth (the strict inequality of two such counts) UNDER-detects when the activity leg of a month is Incomplete while the coverage leg is known: both counts read Incomplete as "not counted". That under-detection is disclosed rather than fixed here, because the returns it could reach are already refused by the W1 completeness member.

Fact.Name: A self-employed enrolled month that is not a coverage month
Fact.Description:
Residual (ix) of the Publication 974 simplified calculation method, and its ONLY detector: whether the return carries at least one month in which the filer was self-employed with no subsidised employer plan available AND was enrolled in a Marketplace policy AND that month is NOT a coverage month on the Form 1095-A.
WHY IT REFUSES. Publication 974 puts the premium for such a month in the NONSPECIFIED bucket (p974 :3074-3075, "Premiums paid for a qualified health plan other than during a coverage month"), which means it belongs on Form 7206 line 1 rather than on Worksheet W line 1. This dictionary asks for line 1 as a single typed Dollar and cannot split a Marketplace policy premium by month, so on this population the two buckets cannot be separated and the return is refused rather than filed with the month silently dropped from both. The slice is rare: a month enrolled but with the premium unpaid, or another source of minimum essential coverage while self-employed.
WHY THE TEST IS A COUNT COMPARISON, NOT A NEW PER-MONTH FACT. /pub974SpecifiedMonthCount already counts the 162(l) months that ARE coverage months and /pub974SelfEmployedEnrolledMonthCount counts the 162(l) months the policy was active in. A coverage month is a subset of an active month, so the strict inequality IS the existence test; twelve more per-month facts would re-derive a quantity the graph already holds. One quantity, one fact.

Fact.Name: The Publication 974 simplified calculation method applies
Fact.Description:
THE SELECTOR for Publication 974's Simplified Calculation Method for Determining the Self-Employed Health Insurance Deduction and Premium Tax Credit (p974 :3460-3530). True exactly on the population this dictionary can run the method for: a filer subject to self-employment tax who paid health insurance premiums under exactly one attested plan business, who carries a Form 1095-A qualified health plan, who is not disqualified from the premium tax credit for a NON-income reason, whose section 162(l) month set and coverage-family question are answered, who has at least one specified-premium month, and for whom none of the coordination residual holds.
WHY EACH CONJUNCT IS HERE, in the plan's own order (plan v2 section B.1). The first four are the section 162(l) admission set this dictionary already uses for Schedule 1 line 17 and are taken verbatim from scheduleSE:/selfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction's own guard, so a return this selector admits is a return that guard would also admit. The premium tax credit conjuncts are the three NON-income tests (/maybeEligibleForPtc, /notPtcApplicableTaxPayerSoFar, /filerNotQualifiedForPtcBecauseOfStatusAndResidenceInfo): the INCOME test cannot sit here, because household income is a function of the deduction this method computes, so an income-based disqualification is a knockout-only stop (scheduleSE:/pub974CannotTakePtcStop) and never a selector. The last conjunct is the coordination residual, read as "Complete and false" rather than as a bare Not, so a residual that is Incomplete on some return leaves this selector Complete FALSE and the return in its existing refusal instead of poisoning Schedule 1 line 17.
WHAT BEING FALSE MEANS. It does NOT mean $0. It means the return is not taken out of scheduleSE:/knockoutSelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction's fourth arm, so the return is refused rather than filed with an uncoordinated deduction. The one exception is the fallback population (/pub974FallbackApplies), which Publication 974 handles by its own prescription rather than by this method.
WHAT STILL READS NOTHING. As of stage 1c this selector is not yet an operand of Schedule 1 line 17: the simplified method's own line 17 is Step 3 line 11, which needs the interim Form 8962 pass, and both are unbuilt. It IS the operand of /pub974WorksheetXApplies and of the Form 8962 line 28 override, and it carries Export downstreamFacts until the Step 3 arm lands.
A LONG-TERM-CARE PREMIUM DOES NOT KEEP A RETURN OUT. Publication 974 calls it a nonspecified premium, figures it on Form 7206 instead of Worksheet P, and carries Form 7206 line 14 into Worksheet W line 14, so a return whose Form 7206 line 2 is banded off each covered person's age (/form7206Line2LongTermCarePremiumsBandedFromCoveredPersons) is admitted. An attested long-term-care premium that is not banded still keeps the selector false. An S-corporation plan still keeps it false: Worksheet W line 11 exists for it, but this selector's first conjunct requires self-employment tax and its plan-business conjunct counts only Schedule C, partnership K-1 and Schedule F businesses, so the more-than-2-percent shareholder is not admitted.

Fact.Name: Publication 974 Worksheet X is completed
Fact.Description:
Whether the return completes Worksheet X. Publication 974 states the test in one sentence: Worksheet X is filled out "only if APTC was paid to your insurer on your behalf for the months you were self-employed" (p974 :3199-3200). The publication's OWN operational form of that test is Worksheet W line 18, "Is line 2 blank or -0-?" - line 2 being the advance payments attributable to the specified premiums - with Yes meaning skip Worksheet X (p974 :3185-3188). So this fact is the method selector AND the negation of Worksheet W line 18; no new arithmetic is minted for it, because the publication already computed the test.
WHAT IT IS FOR. Two consumers, both outside Worksheet X itself: Step 1 chooses between Worksheet X line 31 and Worksheet W line 17 as the deduction it figures household income at (which /pub974Step1SelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction already does off Worksheet W line 18 directly), and the Form 8962 line 28 override applies only to a return that completed Worksheet X and line 25 on it (p974 :3246-3250, "Also, enter this amount on line 28 of the Form 8962 you attach to your tax return if you are required to complete that line and you do not complete Worksheet Y").
COMPLETENESS. /pub974WorksheetWLine18NoAttributableAptc is an Equal over Worksheet W line 2, which is Incomplete when the Form 1095-A is not complete; the method selector is Complete on every return, and an All is Complete false as soon as any conjunct is Complete false, so on a return the method does not admit this fact is Complete false whatever line 18 does. On an admitted return line 18 resolves.

Fact.Name: Publication 974's fallback route for a Marketplace filer who cannot take the credit
Fact.Description:
Whether the return takes Publication 974's FALLBACK route rather than the simplified calculation method. The publication's words are "Cannot take the PTC. If you are not eligible to take the PTC, stop here. Do not use this method. Instead, figure your self-employed health insurance deduction using the Self-Employed Health Insurance Deduction Worksheet in the Instructions for Form 1040 or the Instructions for Form 1040-NR; or, if required, Form 7206." (p974 :3521-3526). The publication PRESCRIBES a computation for this filer; it does not refuse them, and before this change this dictionary did, through scheduleSE:/knockoutSelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction's fourth arm.
WHAT THE FALLBACK COMPUTES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. The prescribed answer is the ORDINARY Form 7206 - /form7206Line14SelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction on an unrestricted line 1 - and NOT a bespoke Schedule 1 line 17 quantity. Two corrections of this fact's first draft follow from that, both of them review findings. (1) There is no /pub974FallbackLine17 twin any more. The twin added Worksheet W line 1 to a line 3 it did not change, so the freed return printed a Form 7206 whose line 14 contradicted its own Schedule 1 line 17 by the whole Marketplace premium, on a form the return always attaches (/form7206RequiredForReturn is true on every return this fact admits, by construction). The Marketplace-exclusion wording on scheduleSE:/writableSelfEmployedHealthInsurancePremiumsPaid is instead RE-SCOPED to the simplified-method population, so on THIS population line 1 carries every premium the filer paid and the ordinary line 14 already is the answer, which is what the paragraph quoted above prescribes. (2) This fact's first draft also said the filer files no Form 8962. That was never true on the return - a filer holding advance payments files Form 8962 Part III and repays at Schedule 2 line 1a - and the clause is struck; the APTC population it was written for is now excluded outright, below. MEASURED after that exclusion, and said precisely because it is easy to mis-read as a vindication of the struck clause: on the admitted population /needsToFileForm8962 is now Complete FALSE and Schedule 2 line 1a is $0. That is a CONSEQUENCE of excluding advance-payment holders, not something Publication 974 says; the publication's paragraph never mentions Form 8962 at all, and no Description or authority comment in this change claims it does.
WHICH INELIGIBILITY. Only the NON-income kind, and that is the whole design constraint. A filer who is ineligible because of filing status, residence or a missing applicability condition is ineligible before household income exists, so the test is computable without the deduction. A filer who is ineligible because household income is below 100 percent of the poverty line with no advance payments, or because /qualifiedForPtc comes out false on the finished return, cannot be detected without running the method first; that population stays a knockout-only refusal (scheduleSE:/pub974CannotTakePtcStop) and is NOT freed here.
NO ADVANCE PAYMENTS, AND THE UNDEFENDED POSITION THAT REFUSAL AVOIDS. A filer who received advance payments of the credit is EXCLUDED - All(IsComplete(ptc:/hasAdvancedPtc), Not(ptc:/hasAdvancedPtc)), written in the refusing direction so that an unknown answer excludes too - and stays in scheduleSE:/pub974CannotTakePtcStop. The reason is stated rather than assumed. Such a filer repays only the CAPPED amount at Schedule 2 line 1a (IRC 36B(f)(2)(B)), so part of the enrollment premium was borne by the Treasury and never repaid, and NO source this repository holds - not Publication 974, not the 2025 Instructions for Form 7206, not IRC 162(l) - says whether that unrepaid part is an "amount paid" by the taxpayer within IRC 162(l)(1). p974 :2986-2993 permits any method whose deduction plus credit does not exceed the enrollment premiums, which is satisfied trivially at a zero credit and so does not settle it either. Rather than take an undefended position on a real dollar amount, this fact refuses.
AT LEAST ONE SPECIFIED MONTH, and the risk it guards is an OVERSTATEMENT. GreaterThanOrEqual( /pub974SpecifiedMonthCount, 1) is required, matching /pub974SimplifiedMethodApplies. On this route the filer types every premium into Form 7206 line 1 having applied the employer-plan month exclusion themselves, exactly as the printed form's own bullet asks. An ANSWERED-EMPTY section 162(l) month set is that same filer saying, on the very next screen, that NO month of 2025 was both self-employed and free of employer-subsidised coverage. The two answers contradict each other, and if the month set is the true one then IRC 162(l)(2)(B) (26 U.S.C. 162, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section162&num=0&edition=2024, RIGHT column) allows nothing at all while this tree would file the whole typed figure. The tree cannot tell a deliberate zero from a click-through, so it refuses: the return falls back to knockout arm 4 and is NAMED there by scheduleSE:/pub974CoordinationResidual member (xv). It is a data-completeness residue, which is the correct permanent refusal, not a computation.
THE REST OF THE ADMISSION SET IS CONSERVATIVE, NOT ARITHMETIC, and this paragraph replaces a first draft that said the opposite. The month set's completeness, Worksheet W line 1's completeness, the coverage-family answer, the single Form 1095-A, the absence of a Part IV allocation and the absence of a QSEHRA were justified as conditions "the fallback arithmetic itself needs". After correction (1) the fallback arithmetic reads NONE of them - it is the ordinary Form 7206 line 14, and the specified premiums do not enter it. They are kept deliberately anyway, as a conservative admission gate: each is a shape whose interaction with IRC 162(l) this change has not measured, and refusing is the only direction that cannot print a wrong number. Each is therefore a NAMED residue a later author may free, one fixture apiece. What this fact deliberately does NOT require is residuals (x) to (xiv) - social security benefits, IRA distributions, employer adoption benefits, Schedule E activity, a traditional IRA contribution - because every one of those exists to protect Worksheet X line 1's household-income BOUND, and the fallback route completes no Worksheet X at all.
COMPLETENESS. Every conjunct is either an IsComplete (always Complete) or is read after one, and an All is Complete false as soon as any conjunct is Complete false, so this fact is Complete on every return that answers the self-employment tax and premiums-paid questions. Its two consumers nonetheless read it as All(IsComplete(x), x), so an Incomplete here refuses rather than files.

Fact.Name: Step 3 Worksheet line 4: months someone in the coverage family was enrolled
Fact.Description:
Step 3 Worksheet LINE 4: how many of the twelve months of 2025 someone in the coverage family was enrolled in the qualified health plan. It is the denominator of line 5, whose numerator is /pub974SpecifiedMonthCount.
THE STEP 3 WORKSHEET, quoted once and referred to by every fact in this block. p974 :3467-3514, RIGHT column: "Step 3 / Figure your self-employed health insurance deduction by completing the following worksheet." Line 1 Worksheet W line 1; line 2 the total PTC from the Step 2 Form 8962 line 24; line 3 the number of months specified premiums were paid; line 4 the number of months someone in the coverage family was enrolled; line 5 line 3 divided by line 4; line 6 line 5 times line 2; line 7 line 1 less line 6; line 8 Worksheet X line 30, or Worksheet W line 16 if Worksheet X was not completed; line 9 the smaller of line 7 or line 8; line 10 Worksheet W line 14; line 11 lines 9 and 10 added, "Use this amount as your self-employed health insurance deduction in Step 4 next. Also, enter this amount on line 17 of Schedule 1 (Form 1040).".
WHY IT IS A NEW FACT AND NOT A READ. ptc names no RETURN-level count of coverage months, which is why this fact exists. THE PER-POLICY COUNT EXISTS: ptc:/1095As/*/numberOfCoverageMonths (ptc.xml:7216) is the same twelve Counts added, one policy at a time. It is not read here for one mechanical reason, stated so a later author does not re-open the question and then re-mint anyway: rolling a per-item Int up to the return needs a CollectionSum over an Int, and there is no CollectionSum over an Int anywhere in dictionary/ty2025 - every one of them sums Dollars. On the admitted population the two agree exactly, because scheduleSE:/pub974CoordinationResidual member (iii) refuses ptc:/hasMultiple1095As, so there is one policy and this fact's outer >= 1 clamp is inert. If an aggregation idiom for Ints ever lands, THIS FACT SHOULD BE RETIRED in favour of the shipping per-policy count summed - that is the one-quantity-one-fact answer and it is only the idiom that blocks it. The count is built here the way /pub974SpecifiedMonthCount and /pub974SelfEmployedEnrolledMonthCount are built - twelve Counts added - so all three read the same way and can be compared without a conversion.
WHY A MONTH IS COUNTED ONCE, not once per policy. The inner Count is compared to 1 before the outer Count wraps it, so a month in which two policies were both coverage months contributes 1, not 2. The publication asks for "the number of months", and this is a division's denominator: counting a month twice would halve line 5 and understate the PTC allocable to the specified premiums. It is a distinction without a difference on the admitted population, which scheduleSE:/pub974CoordinationResidual member (iii) restricts to a single Form 1095-A, but the arithmetic is written for the general case because a later author who narrows (iii) must not have to re-find this.
COMPLETE-SAFETY. A Count resolves an Incomplete operand to 0, and an Add of twelve Counts is therefore Complete on EVERY return, including one with no /1095As collection at all, where it is 0. The consequence a later author must not undo, exactly as on /pub974SelfEmployedEnrolledMonthCount: Not(IsComplete(this fact)) is identically false and is dead as a detector. Zero here means "no coverage month is known", which is indistinguishable from "nothing was asked", and the data-completeness residue for that is carried by Not(IsComplete(/pub974WorksheetWLine1SpecifiedPremiums)) and member (xv) in scheduleSE:/pub974CoordinationResidual.

Fact.Name: Step 3 Worksheet lines 5 and 6: the interim PTC allocable to the specified premiums
Fact.Description:
Step 3 Worksheet LINES 5 AND 6 FOLDED: the part of the interim premium tax credit that is allocable to the specified premiums. Line 5 (line 3 divided by line 4) is a bare ratio with no other consumer, so it is not minted as a fact of its own; line 6 is line 5 times line 2, computed here as Round(interim line 24 x specified months / coverage months) so that the division happens once, in the rounding the publication's own worksheet does at the end.
THE STEP 3 WORKSHEET, quoted once and referred to by every fact in this block. p974 :3467-3514, RIGHT column: "Step 3 / Figure your self-employed health insurance deduction by completing the following worksheet." Line 1 Worksheet W line 1; line 2 the total PTC from the Step 2 Form 8962 line 24; line 3 the number of months specified premiums were paid; line 4 the number of months someone in the coverage family was enrolled; line 5 line 3 divided by line 4; line 6 line 5 times line 2; line 7 line 1 less line 6; line 8 Worksheet X line 30, or Worksheet W line 16 if Worksheet X was not completed; line 9 the smaller of line 7 or line 8; line 10 Worksheet W line 14; line 11 lines 9 and 10 added, "Use this amount as your self-employed health insurance deduction in Step 4 next. Also, enter this amount on line 17 of Schedule 1 (Form 1040).".
THE CAUTION UNDER LINE 1, and it is the reason this fact has three cases rather than one. p974 :3481-3488: "If the amounts on lines 12 through 23, column (e), of your Step 2 Form 8962 are not the same for each month and you had specified premiums for less than 12 months, skip lines 2 through 5 below and enter on line 6 the total of those column (e) amounts for the months you paid specified premiums." Both conditions must hold. When they do, this fact sums ptc:/pub974InterimMonthlyPtcAllowedFor{M} over the months /pub974SpecifiedMonth{M} calls specified, which is the publication's instruction taken literally; ptc:/pub974InterimMonthlyAllowedIsUniform carries the first condition and this fact carries the second. Proration is only right when every month carries the same credit, which is exactly what the Caution says.
THE ZERO-DENOMINATOR CASE is structural, not a tax rule: it makes the fact total on a return with no coverage month at all, where line 2 is $0 anyway so $0 is also the arithmetic answer. It is unreachable on the admitted population, because form7206:/pub974SimplifiedMethodApplies requires at least one specified month and a specified month IS a coverage month, so line 4 is at least 1 there.
WHY LINE 6 CANNOT EXCEED LINE 1, which is what keeps line 7 non-negative without a floor the publication does not print. On the Caution route line 6 sums column (e) amounts over the specified months, and each column (e) is the LESSER of that month's enrollment premium and the maximum assistance (IRC 36B(b)(2)), so line 6 is at most the enrollment premiums for those months, which is line 1. On the proration route the Caution did not fire, so either every column (e) is equal - and then line 2 / line 4 is one month's credit, so line 6 is that credit times the specified months, again at most the premiums for those months - or the specified-month count is 12, in which case line 4 is 12 too (a specified month is a coverage month) and line 6 is the whole of line 2, at most the whole of line 1. Line 7 is therefore never negative on any return this method admits.
COMPLETE-SAFETY. The Switch has a True default; each Caution addend reads an Incomplete month as $0; the proration case reads two counts that are Complete on every return and an interim line 24 that is Complete whenever ptc:/hasPtcQualifyingPlan is, which the method selector requires.

Fact.Name: Step 3 Worksheet line 7: specified premiums net of the allocable PTC
Fact.Description:
Step 3 Worksheet LINE 7: the specified premiums less the premium tax credit allocable to them - the part of the Marketplace premium the filer actually bore, and so the part IRC 162(l)(1) can allow as a deduction.
THE STEP 3 WORKSHEET, quoted once and referred to by every fact in this block. p974 :3467-3514, RIGHT column: "Step 3 / Figure your self-employed health insurance deduction by completing the following worksheet." Line 1 Worksheet W line 1; line 2 the total PTC from the Step 2 Form 8962 line 24; line 3 the number of months specified premiums were paid; line 4 the number of months someone in the coverage family was enrolled; line 5 line 3 divided by line 4; line 6 line 5 times line 2; line 7 line 1 less line 6; line 8 Worksheet X line 30, or Worksheet W line 16 if Worksheet X was not completed; line 9 the smaller of line 7 or line 8; line 10 Worksheet W line 14; line 11 lines 9 and 10 added, "Use this amount as your self-employed health insurance deduction in Step 4 next. Also, enter this amount on line 17 of Schedule 1 (Form 1040).".
NO FLOOR AT $0, DELIBERATELY. The publication prints a plain "Subtract line 6 from line 1" with no floor, and this fact does the same. The proof that it cannot go negative on any return the method admits is written out on /pub974Step3Line6PtcAllocableToSpecifiedPremiums and turns on column (e) being the LESSER of the month's enrollment premium and the maximum assistance. Adding a floor the source does not print would hide a violation of that argument rather than prevent one. OFF THE ADMITTED POPULATION IT DOES GO NEGATIVE, and that is measured rather than assumed (review-K1-stage1d, item 4): on a return whose self-employment earnings fall under $400 - so Worksheet W line 1 collapses while the interim credit does not - this line and Step 3 line 11 came back MINUS 2,200.00. It reaches nothing: scheduleSE:/selfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction reads Step 3 line 11 only under All(IsComplete(selector), selector), and that return is selector-false. The sentence is here for the author who one day WIDENS the selector: the non-negativity proof above is a proof about the admitted population only, and widening the selector means re-proving it or adding the floor.
COMPLETE-SAFETY. Line 6 is Complete on every return. Line 1 is Incomplete when the Form 1095-A cannot resolve the specified premiums, and that is deliberate and load-bearing: it is the detector scheduleSE:/pub974CoordinationResidual member (vii) reads, so such a return is refused by the knockout rather than reaching this arithmetic.

Fact.Name: Step 3 Worksheet line 8: Worksheet X line 30, or Worksheet W line 16
Fact.Description:
Step 3 Worksheet LINE 8: the ceiling the specified-premium deduction is capped at - Worksheet X line 30 on a return that completed Worksheet X, Worksheet W line 16 on a return that did not.
THE STEP 3 WORKSHEET, quoted once and referred to by every fact in this block. p974 :3467-3514, RIGHT column: "Step 3 / Figure your self-employed health insurance deduction by completing the following worksheet." Line 1 Worksheet W line 1; line 2 the total PTC from the Step 2 Form 8962 line 24; line 3 the number of months specified premiums were paid; line 4 the number of months someone in the coverage family was enrolled; line 5 line 3 divided by line 4; line 6 line 5 times line 2; line 7 line 1 less line 6; line 8 Worksheet X line 30, or Worksheet W line 16 if Worksheet X was not completed; line 9 the smaller of line 7 or line 8; line 10 Worksheet W line 14; line 11 lines 9 and 10 added, "Use this amount as your self-employed health insurance deduction in Step 4 next. Also, enter this amount on line 17 of Schedule 1 (Form 1040).".
THE SWITCH IS /pub974WorksheetXApplies AND NOTHING ELSE. That fact was built by stage 1c to be exactly this test: it is the method selector conjoined with the negation of Worksheet W line 18 ("Is line 2 blank or -0-? Yes. Skip line 19 and Worksheet X"), which is the publication's own operational form of "Complete this worksheet only if APTC was paid to your insurer on your behalf for the months you were self-employed" (p974 :3200, :3185-3188). Re-deriving the test here would be a second spelling of one quantity.
COMPLETE-SAFETY. The Switch has a True default and /pub974WorksheetXApplies is Complete on every return (its first conjunct is the method selector, and an All is Complete false as soon as any conjunct is). The fallback branch is Worksheet W line 16, which is the LesserOf of two facts that the same population resolves.

Fact.Name: Step 3 Worksheet line 9: the smaller of line 7 and line 8
Fact.Description:
Step 3 Worksheet LINE 9: the smaller of line 7 and line 8 - the specified-premium half of the deduction, after both the credit subtraction and the earned-income ceiling.
THE STEP 3 WORKSHEET, quoted once and referred to by every fact in this block. p974 :3467-3514, RIGHT column: "Step 3 / Figure your self-employed health insurance deduction by completing the following worksheet." Line 1 Worksheet W line 1; line 2 the total PTC from the Step 2 Form 8962 line 24; line 3 the number of months specified premiums were paid; line 4 the number of months someone in the coverage family was enrolled; line 5 line 3 divided by line 4; line 6 line 5 times line 2; line 7 line 1 less line 6; line 8 Worksheet X line 30, or Worksheet W line 16 if Worksheet X was not completed; line 9 the smaller of line 7 or line 8; line 10 Worksheet W line 14; line 11 lines 9 and 10 added, "Use this amount as your self-employed health insurance deduction in Step 4 next. Also, enter this amount on line 17 of Schedule 1 (Form 1040).".
WHAT THE TWO OPERANDS EACH GUARD. Line 7 is the IRC 162(l)(1) "amount paid" limit: the filer may not deduct a premium the Treasury paid through the credit. Line 8 is the IRC 162(l)(2)(A) earned-income limit, net of the nonspecified-premium deduction Worksheet W line 14 already used up. Taking the smaller is what makes the sum of the deduction and the credit at most the enrollment premiums, which is the rule p974 :2988-2993 states for any acceptable method.
COMPLETE-SAFETY. Both operands resolve on the admitted population; line 7 is Incomplete exactly when Worksheet W line 1 is, which is the refused data-completeness residue.

Fact.Name: Step 3 Worksheet line 11: the simplified method's Schedule 1 line 17
Fact.Description:
Step 3 Worksheet LINE 11, AND THE WHOLE POINT OF THE SERIES: the self-employed health insurance deduction the Simplified Calculation Method figures. "Add lines 9 and 10. Use this amount as your self-employed health insurance deduction in Step 4 next. Also, enter this amount on line 17 of Schedule 1 (Form 1040)." (p974 :3511-3514). scheduleSE:/selfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction reads this fact on the population form7206:/pub974SimplifiedMethodApplies admits, and that arm is what frees the population scheduleSE:/knockoutSelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction's fourth arm has been refusing.
THE STEP 3 WORKSHEET, quoted once and referred to by every fact in this block. p974 :3467-3514, RIGHT column: "Step 3 / Figure your self-employed health insurance deduction by completing the following worksheet." Line 1 Worksheet W line 1; line 2 the total PTC from the Step 2 Form 8962 line 24; line 3 the number of months specified premiums were paid; line 4 the number of months someone in the coverage family was enrolled; line 5 line 3 divided by line 4; line 6 line 5 times line 2; line 7 line 1 less line 6; line 8 Worksheet X line 30, or Worksheet W line 16 if Worksheet X was not completed; line 9 the smaller of line 7 or line 8; line 10 Worksheet W line 14; line 11 lines 9 and 10 added, "Use this amount as your self-employed health insurance deduction in Step 4 next. Also, enter this amount on line 17 of Schedule 1 (Form 1040).".
LINE 10 IS THE SHIPPING FORM 7206 LINE 14, and that is a reading of the source, not a shortcut. Step 3 line 10 says "Enter the amount from Worksheet W, line 14", and Worksheet W line 14 says "Enter your self-employed health insurance deduction for NONSPECIFIED premiums from Worksheet P, line 3, or Form 7206, line 14" (p974 :3180-3181). On the admitted population Form 7206 line 1 is scheduleSE:/writableSelfEmployedHealthInsurancePremiumsPaid, whose wording was re-scoped by stage 1c to exclude the Marketplace premiums that the 1095-A carries, so the shipping line 14 IS the nonspecified-premium deduction and no twin is needed. /pub974WorksheetWLine15EarnedIncomeLimitNetOfNonspecified and /pub974WorksheetWLine17TotalDeductionLimit already read it the same way.
WHY THIS FACT AND NOT WORKSHEET W LINE 17. Worksheet W line 17 (line 14 plus line 16) is the answer for a filer who skipped Worksheet X, and Step 1 reads it for exactly that purpose. It is NOT the Schedule 1 line 17 answer, because it has not subtracted the premium tax credit: line 7 above is where the credit comes out. The two facts differ by line 6 on every return that receives a credit, and confusing them would deduct premiums the Treasury paid.
COMPLETE-SAFETY. An Add of two facts that both resolve on the admitted population. /form7206Line14SelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction is the shipping fact the ordinary Schedule 1 line 17 arm already reads on this same return, so it cannot be Incomplete here without being Incomplete there.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 iterative method: household income before any self-employed health insurance deduction
Fact.Description: Household income with the self-employed health insurance deduction taken back out: Step 1's household income plus the Step 1 deduction it was figured at. Every round of the iterative method subtracts its own trial deduction from this figure, which is how each Step 4 pass figures household income at "the total of the Step 3 Worksheet, line 9, and Worksheet W, line 14" (or, from the second round on, the previous round's Step 5 line 7) without reading the shipping household income (that one is built on the deduction this method solves for, so reading it would be a cycle).

Fact.Name: Pub. 974: the Step 3 Worksheet skipped lines 2 through 5
Fact.Description: True when the Step 3 Worksheet took its line 1 Caution route (the Step 2 monthly column (e) amounts are not all equal and there are fewer than 12 specified months) and so entered on line 6 the column (e) total for the specified months. The Step 5 Worksheet follows the same route ("If you skipped lines 2 through 5 of the Step 3 Worksheet, skip lines 2 and 3 below and enter on line 4 the total of the column (e) amounts from your Step 4 Form 8962 for the months you paid specified premiums"). Same three tests, in the same order, as /pub974Step3Line6PtcAllocableToSpecifiedPremiums.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 iterative method: January takes a Form 8962 column (e) amount
Fact.Description: Whether January is a month the refigured Form 8962 fills column (e) for on the monthly route: the same four conditions the interim pass tests on ptc:/pub974InterimMonthlyPtcAllowedForJan (a qualifying plan, the monthly route, an active policy, and no policy losing the month to the premium-paid rule). It does not depend on household income, so every round reads it.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 iterative method: January SLCSP premium (Form 8962 column (b))
Fact.Description: The January applicable SLCSP premium summed over the return's Form 1095-A policies, entered in whole dollars as the interim pass enters it. It is an input to every round, not a computed amount, so the no-rounding caution does not reach it.

Fact.Name: Pub. 974 iterative method: January enrollment premium (Form 8962 column (a))
